El Proyecto plantea importantes reformas al Código Tributario, así como a la Ley de Régimen Tributario Interno.

¿Cuáles son los principales cambios?

En el Código Tributario de 1975, se introducen los siguientes cambios:

Reformas generales

- Se agrega un nuevo derecho del contribuyente: los cambios de criterio interpretativo de alcance general tendrán que publicarse en una norma, y regirán solo hacia el futuro, salvo que sean más favorables.

- Se aclara que el Código Tributario tiene la naturaleza de ley orgánica.

- Se actualiza la denominación de los tribunales fiscales por "Tribunales Distritales de lo Contencioso Tributario", denominación que mantienen desde la expedición del Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial en 2009.

Reformas relativas al valor de los actos normativos de la administración tributaria

- Se puntualiza que las circulares obligarán solo a los funcionarios y no serán vinculantes para los contribuyentes.

- Se dispone que las fichas técnicas, manuales, instructivos y criterios internos de las administraciones tributarias, no podrán crear, modificar ni extinguir obligaciones, exenciones ni beneficios.

Reformas relativas a notificaciones

- Se aclara que la Administración tendrá que usar primero el medio de notificación que el contribuyente haya señalado en el expediente (por ejemplo, correo o casillero judicial) y se dispone que solo podrá usar otro medio si existe una imposibilidad técnica justificada.

- Se precisa que la notificación electrónica se hará por el buzón del contribuyente y por los correos que este haya señalado.

Sobre las solicitudes, reclamos y la determinación complementaria

- Se aclara que los sujetos pasivos pueden presentar reclamos contra todo tipo de actos administrativos emanados de las administraciones tributarias (actualmente el Código se refiere solamente a “actos determinativos”.

- Se aclara que la determinación complementaria es un proceso que puede iniciarse únicamente en el trámite de reclamos (no de solicitudes).

- Aunque se mantiene el plazo de 120 días hábiles desde el día siguiente a la presentación como término para la resolución de reclamos, se clarifica que las solicitudes de información que se realicen en el trámite de los mismos, tendrán que hacerse dentro de 60 días y se dispone que la suspensión que puede ordenarse por este motivo, en ningún caso podrá superar 90 días ni ocurrir más de una vez.

- Respecto a la solicitudes de devolución de pago en exceso, se dispone que el término para resolverlas será de 120 días (actualmente se establece un plazo de 6 meses) y en caso de negativa, se aclara que el sujeto pasivo acudir directamente a las acciones judiciales del COGEP.

Sobre el recurso de revisión

Se dispone que si el interesado presenta el recurso, la Administración estará obligada a admitirlo, tramitarlo y emitir una resolución motivada. Hoy se trata como una facultad potestativa de la administración.

- Se fijan requisitos de admisibilidad:

Los mismos exigidos para la presentación del reclamo, conforme al artículo 119 del Código Tributario; y además:

- - La determinación de las causales en que se funda.

- - El anuncio probatorio, cuando corresponda.

- Si el escrito que contiene el recurso de revisión es oscuro o incompleto, se concede 10 días para aclararlo o completarlo.

- Se modifican los plazos d

item.title: As mortgage rates rise, more borrowers are turning to adjustable-rate loans
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
As mortgage rates rise, more borrowers are turning to adjustable-rate loans
2026-10-09
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/as-mortgage-rates-rise-more-borrowers-are-turning-to-adjustable-rate-loans-171507956.html
As mortgage rates approach 8%, more buyers are turning to adjustable-rate mortgages to save on interest.
Nearly 11% of mortgage borrowers who locked in a rate in mid-September opted for an ARM, according to ICE Mortgage Technology data. The share is up more than three percentage points over the past three months to the highest in nearly four years.
ARMs can offer meaningful rate savings over a 30-year fixed-rate loan, but there's a catch: Instead of locking in one rate for the entire 30-year term, borrowers commit to an initial, often lower rate for a shorter period, typically five or seven years. After the initial term is up, their rate adjusts based on market conditions once or twice a year.
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
In the chart above, "rate lock activity" refers to borrowers locking in a rate after applying for a mortgage. Refinancings are leading the trend, likely driven by owners who took out a fixed-rate loan above 7% and those needing to cash out some of their equity.
Many borrowers think the rate gamble is worth it: While the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is around 7.63% on Wednesday, a 7/6 ARM — which carries a fixed term for seven years and then adjusts every six months — is 6.95%, according to Mortgage News Daily.
Many borrowers who seek out ARMs intend to sell their home before their initial fixed-rate term expires. Others are effectively betting that rates will be lower in the future, allowing them to refinance.
Most borrowers who took out ARMs in 2022 and 2023, when rates first started moving higher, remain in their initial fixed-rate period, meaning the Fed's recent tightening hasn't affected their rates. While 30-year fixed mortgage rates aren't directly influenced by the Fed, ARMs in their adjustment rates are much more sensitive to the central bank's interest rate decisions.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
Carlos Rojas
October 7, 2026
Si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos.
1.- Porque igual a cómo sucedió con Rafael Correa, hace diez años, se reedita una peligrosa pelea entre el gobierno de turno, intolerante a la crítica y la fiscalización, y la prensa independiente, pilar de cualquier democracia liberal.
2.- Porque el tránsito que irremediablemente debe dar un medio tradicional hacia formatos digitales es muy complejo y costoso, por lo que las presiones políticas, judiciales y financieras externas restan oxígeno y fuerza a ese momento.
3.- Porque si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos. Decenas de periodistas y líderes de opinión que años atrás libraron una verdadera batalla por las libertades hoy callan, acomodados al financiamiento que el poder decidió otorgarles a cambio de su obsecuencia.
4.- Porque el papel de las élites, en especial de los empresarios, luce apagado, desorientado y sin entender que los referentes democráticos son esenciales para el desarrollo nacional. Y allí el patrocinio del trabajo de la prensa libre es fundamental.
5.- Porque a la gente, en general, parece preocuparle muy poco que el espacio de la prensa independiente esté cada vez más reducido, mientras las falencias institucionales y de gestión del Gobierno ameritan amplios espacios de fiscalización.
Lo que está ocurriendo con diario Expreso es un síntoma muy grave de que la salud democrática del Ecuador anda mal. Empeora.

Lo que está ocurriendo con diario Expreso es un síntoma muy grave de que la salud democrática del Ecuador anda mal. Empeora.

Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
Carlos Rojas
October 7, 2026
Si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos.
1.- Porque igual a cómo sucedió con Rafael Correa, hace diez años, se reedita una peligrosa pelea entre el gobierno de turno, intolerante a la crítica y la fiscalización, y la prensa independiente, pilar de cualquier democracia liberal.
2.- Porque el tránsito que irremediablemente debe dar un medio tradicional hacia formatos digitales es muy complejo y costoso, por lo que las presiones políticas, judiciales y financieras externas restan oxígeno y fuerza a ese momento.
3.- Porque si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos. Decenas de periodistas y líderes de opinión que años atrás libraron una verdadera batalla por las libertades hoy callan, acomodados al financiamiento que el poder decidió otorgarles a cambio de su obsecuencia.
4.- Porque el papel de las élites, en especial de los empresarios, luce apagado, desorientado y sin entender que los referentes democráticos son esenciales para el desarrollo nacional. Y allí el patrocinio del trabajo de la prensa libre es fundamental.
5.- Porque a la gente, en general, parece preocuparle muy poco que el espacio de la prensa independiente esté cada vez más reducido, mientras las falencias institucionales y de gestión del Gobierno ameritan amplios espacios de fiscalización.

item.title: María Paz Jervis tenía razon
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
María Paz Jervis tenía razon
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Empresarios: María Paz Jervis tenía razón
Carlos Rojas
October 2, 2026
Es una lástima que un país los industriales y empresarios no logren tener una posición clara, respetuosa, digna y firme frente a un gobierno cuyas decisiones los afecta profundamente.
En el marco de la celebración por los 90 años de la CIP, María Paz Jervis dijo sentirse sorprendida y desesperanzada por ver a un sector empresarial “con tanto miedo”. Miedo -insistió- a defender la libertad de expresión, los valores democráticos y a pensar que disentir con las decisiones que toma el Gobierno no es convertirse en enemigos.
Estas declaraciones, que cayeron muy mal en todo el gremio a escala nacional, se dieron a la par de las disposiciones del Ministerio de Energía para que las grandes industrias tengan un día de desconexión eléctrica.
El alboroto que se desató en redes sociales coincidió con la renuncia de Jervis a la presidencia de la Cámara, mientras en los canales de televisión y las redes sociales, otros dirigentes de este sector decían que es mejor tener un diálogo constructivo con el Régimen pues la crisis energética debe ser resuelta con el apoyo de todos.
No faltaron las críticas a Jervis de parte los periodistas-voceros del Ejecutivo, aquellos que, desde sus radios, justifican cada una de las decisiones del Presidente, al punto de que sus comentarios terminan convertidos en verdaderas tomaduras de pelo para sus audiencias. Claro, celebraban la renuncia de la dirigente como la consecuencia natural de lo que calificaron como un error de bulto: hablar por los empresarios bajo criterios que eran únicamente suyos.
Tres doritos después, la cruda realidad meteorológica y el inconmovible pragmatismo del presidente Noboa demostraron que Jervis no estaba del todo equivocada. Es decir, que el temor no garantiza un buen trato.
En seis días, la orden de desconexión pasó de un día a tres por semana; y en Durán, el racionamiento para las grandes industrias será de cuatro.
Al inicio, el plan del Ministerio de Energía era afectar a 182 de esas empresas, pero para el viernes subieron a casi nueve mil. Como si esto no fuera suficiente, hasta les incrementaron de forma drástica la tarifa eléctrica.
Semejante paquetazo obligó a la Cámara de Industrias de Guayaquil, primero, y a la que presidía Jervis, después, a emitir sendos comunicados que tendrán cero efectos reales, ante un Régimen que no está acostumbrado a retroceder.
Es una lástima que un país donde los industriales y empresarios quisieron tumbar a Osvaldo Hurtado; marcaron el ascenso político e influyeron con sus tesis en el gobierno de Febres Cordero; o arrinconaron a Bucaram, Mahuad y Gutiérrez en sus horas difíciles, sean hoy incapaces de tener una posición clara, respetuosa, digna y firme frente a un gobierno que preferirá apagar a todo el sector productivo creyendo que con ello no cortará la luz de los millones de hogares en vísperas de unas elecciones donde el poder político de ADN está en juego. La ingenuidad de los empresarios le costará algunos puntos del PIB.

item.title: Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
By Carlos Rojas
October 9, 2026
Al Presidente le hicieron cometer tremendo error, el lunes a primera hora, cuando prometió públicamente en una de las radios, cuya línea editorial está bajo su control, que no habría apagones en los hogares ecuatorianos.
El presidente Daniel Noboa durante el evento por la Independencia de Guayaquil en el Coliseo Voltaire Paladines Polo. Foto: API
El presidente Daniel Noboa durante el evento por la Independencia de Guayaquil en el Coliseo Voltaire Paladines Polo. Foto: API
Cuando los asesores de un presidente construyen la estrategia política de su gobierno sobre la base de un espejismo, se exponen a que esta, más temprano que tarde, se invalide al primer choque con la realidad.
A Daniel Noboa le hicieron cometer tremendo error, el lunes a primera hora, cuando prometió públicamente en una de las radios, cuya línea editorial está bajo su control, que no habría apagones en los hogares ecuatorianos. La frase fue replicada por el aparato comunicacional de todo Carondelet.
Han pasado casi tres años de mandato, así como tres crisis eléctricas, y en el Ejecutivo no aprenden la lecció n. La realidad no se teje a punta de propaganda ni de deseos formulados sobre la base del capricho. Este jueves, final de una semana corta, los ecuatorianos se van al feriado con una sensación de incertidumbre total, pues las grandes y medianas industrias se desconectarán tres días por semana, cuando el compromiso del Ministerio de Energía, el viernes anterior, era de que los apagones solo fueran de dos días.
Y lo más complejo, el martes en Guayaquil y este día en Quito, varios sectores de ambas urbes han reportado cortes no programados de electricidad, mientras las pantallas de la Celec muestran el caudal de Mazar cayendo en picada.
Con miles de hogares sin luz en ciertas horas pico de la demanda, así la autoridad eléctrica diga que es por mantenimiento de las redes de transmisión o por el daño en alguna estación, lo único que conseguirá el Gobierno es que la gente ponga en duda la promesa del Presidente y su palabra se devalúe.
Los asesores, funcionarios y periodistas áulicos de su despacho hacen mal en insertar al Jefe de Estado en un mundo paralelo, que nada tiene que ver con la realidad que, por otro lado, y por más adversa que esta sea, la prensa retrata todos los días, así la califiquen de odiadora, mala fe o negativa.
Esa desesperación porque la gente mastique sin ningún reparo estas narrativas contradice el supuesto buen momento por el que pasa Noboa según las encuestas (hasta casi 20 puntos, supuestamente recuperados en dos meses).
Tampoco se entiende la desacertada carta que el mandatario difundió la mañana del miércoles 7 de octubre, anunciando que el galón de la Extra, Ecopaís y el diésel bajará cuatro centavos, pese que la economía global tiene que lidiar con un petróleo y sus derivados que están por las nubes.
¿Para qué el Presidente se ancla a anuncios tan controversiales si se supone que todo va bien con su popularidad?
Esa sobrerreacción comunicacional llama la atención sobre manera. Noboa no tardó en colgar en sus redes un video muy corto sobre las obras que tiene para la Universidad de Cuenca, pocas horas después de que los estudiantes lo recibieran mal en su visita a ese centro académico el miércoles.
O que Julio José Neira pusiera todo su talento -que no es mucho, por cierto- a cuestionar el reportaje de Ecuavisa sobre la construcción del hospital del IESS en Cayambe donde, lejos del render propagandístico, apenas hay algún movimiento de tierras.
En fin, esta semana cierra de muy mala manera para un gobierno acostumbrado a los golpes de efecto diarios, pero descuidando el panorama real. Por eso los tropiezos.

item.title: La trampa de las encuestas
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
La trampa de las encuestas
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
La trampa de las encuestas
Por Carlos Rojas
October 6, 2026
Gobernar desde la percepción de las encuestas siempre será un error para cualquier político, tanto en Brasil como Ecuador, donde el voto oculto es un mecanismo de defensa frente al autoritarismo.
Hasta el domingo en la mañana, buena parte de América Latina intuía que Lula da Silva iba a vencer en la primera vuelta y proyectar así la consolidación de su triunfo en la balotaje del 24 de octubre próximo.
Pero su rival, el ultraderechista Flavio Bolsonaro le aguó la fiesta pues, por momentos, parecía que iba a ganar la presidencia en una sola elección.
Si bien eso no ocurrió, el hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro pasó primero al balotaje con casi dos puntos de ventaja, cuando los sondeos de opinión daban a Lula una ventaja de entre cuatro y seis puntos.
Podría decirse, desde la aritmética, que el fallo de las ecuestas no es momumental. Es más, que está dentro de una probalilidad estadística.
Pero en el plano político, el análisis es diferente y profundamente perjudicial para los planes de Lula de acceder a un cuarto período. Haber pasado del primer al segundo lugar, solo porque las encuestas lo midieron mal, es un hecho que desinfla su candidatura y le echará a perder la campaña en la segunda vuelta. Es muy probable ahora, que Flávio Bolsonaro sea elegido presidente, porque ha quedado marcada una tendencia.
De allí que gobernar desde la percepción de las encuestas siempre será un error para cualquier político, tanto en Brasil como Ecuador.
El tema viene a colación porque desde hace un mes, el gobierno del presidente Daniel Noboa asegura que su popularidad ha trepado casi 20 puntos en dos meses consecutivos. Y para ello ha mostrado el trabajo de varias encuestas: CIEES, Click Report, Atlas Intel, entre otras.
No hay razones para no creer que el mandatario se haya fortalecido políticamente, dados sus recientes golpes a las mafias, entre estos la deportación de José Serrano o la captura de Xavier Jordán.
Pero la realidad política de nuestras sociedades es mucho más compleja que cifrar en un número, el nivel de apoyo total a un gobierno. Más aún si la realidad está tan expuesta a crisis y eventos que no son fáciles de controlar como los apagones y la destrucción de las lluvias que traiga El Niño.
En el Gobierno deben estar convencidos que esto es así, por lo que los buenos número de las encuestas sirven más bien para consolidar el aparato de propaganda y que la gente se convenza de que el ambiente favorable es generalizado e irrebatible.
Por eso, la orquestación se nota cuando los medios y periodistas áulicos del Régimen arman sus agendas de trabajo enfocados en esa perspectiva.
Sin embargo, una sociedad donde el voto oculto es un mecanismo de defensa en sistemas que tienden al autoritarismo, estas verdades se desmoronan como castillos de naipes.
item.content:encoded:
La trampa de las encuestas

2026-10-09

Por Texto propio

La trampa de las encuestas

Por Carlos Rojas

October 6, 2026

Gobernar desde la percepción de las encuestas siempre será un error para cualquier político, tanto en Brasil como Ecuador, donde el voto oculto es un mecanismo de defensa frente al autoritarismo.

Hasta el domingo en la mañana, buena parte de América Latina intuía que Lula da Silva iba a vencer en la primera vuelta y proyectar así la consolidación de su triunfo en la balotaje del 24 de octubre próximo.

Pero su rival, el ultraderechista Flavio Bolsonaro le aguó la fiesta pues, por momentos, parecía que iba a ganar la presidencia en una sola elección.

Si bien eso no ocurrió, el hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro pasó primero al balotaje con casi dos puntos de ventaja, cuando los sondeos de opinión daban a Lula una ventaja de entre cuatro y seis puntos.

Podría decirse, desde la aritmética, que el fallo de las ecuestas no es momumental. Es más, que está dentro de una probalilidad estadística.

Pero en el plano político, el análisis es diferente y profundamente perjudicial para los planes de Lula de acceder a un cuarto período. Haber pasado del primer al segundo lugar, solo porque las encuestas lo midieron mal, es un hecho que desinfla su candidatura y le echará a perder la campaña en la segunda vuelta. Es muy probable ahora, que Flávio Bolsonaro sea elegido presidente, porque ha quedado marcada una tendencia.

De allí que gobernar desde la percepción de las encuestas siempre será un error para cualquier político, tanto en Brasil como Ecuador.

El tema viene a colación porque desde hace un mes, el gobierno del presidente Daniel Noboa asegura que su popularidad ha trepado casi 20 puntos en dos meses consecutivos. Y para ello ha mostrado el trabajo de varias encuestas: CIEES, Click Report, Atlas Intel, entre otras.

No hay razones para no creer que el mandatario se haya fortalecido políticamente, dados sus recientes golpes a las mafias, entre estos la deportación de José Serrano o la captura de Xavier Jordán.

Pero la realidad política de nuestras sociedades es mucho más compleja que cifrar en un número, el nivel de apoyo total a un gobierno. Más aún si la realidad está tan expuesta a crisis y eventos que no son fáciles de controlar como los apagones y la destrucción de las lluvias que traiga El Niño.

En el Gobierno deben estar convencidos que esto es así, por lo que los buenos número de las encuestas sirven más bien para consolidar el aparato de propaganda y que la gente se convenza de que el ambiente favorable es generalizado e irrebatible.

Por eso, la orquestación se nota cuando los medios y periodistas áulicos del Régimen arman sus agendas de trabajo enfocados en esa perspectiva.

Sin embargo, una sociedad donde el voto oculto es un mecanismo de defensa en sistemas que tienden al autoritarismo, estas verdades se desmoronan como castillos de naipes.

Good morning. The major averages retreated for a second day in a row, with chip stocks falling.
Long-dated bonds climbed again, and Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) rose toward $105 per barrel amid persistent US-Iran tensions.
The 10-year Treasury (^TNX) yield rose to 5.32%, signaling a tightening of financial conditions as everything from mortgages to car loans and corporate borrowing becomes more expensive.
The market forecasts the Federal Reserve will keep rates unchanged at its October meeting, but raise them in December.

Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Tech (XLK) stocks slipped, with AI chip giants Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) set to decline from their record highs for a second day in a row.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) declined to trade below $83,000 per token.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: Palentir (PLTR), PepsiCo (PEP), and Applied Digital (APLD).

item.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su just struck another bullish note with the stock on fire
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AMD CEO Lisa Su just struck another bullish note with the stock on fire
2026-10-09
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amd-ceo-lisa-su-just-struck-another-bullish-note-with-the-stock-on-fire-101318248.html
AMD (AMD) CEO Lisa Su is dropping bullish nuggets all over the place on her overseas chip tour.
On a visit to Seoul on Wednesday to meet with the likes of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (SKHY), Su said overall data center demand remained "very strong," according to a Reuters report. Su reportedly added that she is seeing "strong demand signals" across AMD's product portfolio.
This comes a day after a trip to Taipei on Tuesday, where she predicted chip demand would stay strong for years.
Shares of AMD are trading at a record high and are up 200% year to date.
The stock has more record highs ahead, in part because of demand for the new Meta (META) AI agent known as Muse, Citi said on Tuesday.
Citi analyst Atif Malik raised his price target on AMD to $800 from $575.
"Following the release of Meta Muse and our subsequent CPU TAM raise, we are raising estimates on AMD given our belief that AMD will be the primary beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and our belief that Meta is one of the largest customers of AMD's server business," Malik said.
Malik also struck a bullish tone on the future size of the CPU market.
"We update our CPU model post the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. Fundamentally, we view agentic AI as a potential orders-of-magnitude driver of compute demand relative to traditional chatbots," Malik added. "We believe the CPU TAM [total addressable market] expands from $29 billion in 2025 to $300 billion in 2030, or a 60% CAGR. We still expect AMD to be the key beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and Intel as a secondary beneficiary."

item.title: The tech industry wants you to run AI models at home, but it’s not for everyone
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
The tech industry wants you to run AI models at home, but it’s not for everyone
2026-10-09
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-tech-industry-wants-you-to-run-ai-models-at-home-but-its-not-for-everyone-195314548.html
Microsoft (MSFT) on Wednesday unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra, designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud.
Starting at $2,599, the Surface Laptop Ultra runs on Nvidia's (NVDA) Arm-based RTX Spark, which offers upwards of 128GB of onboard memory.
Most consumers and enterprise users access AI platforms through cloud services like OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) ChatGPT, Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude, Google's (GOOG, GOOGL) Gemini, or Meta's (META) Muse. Microsoft and Nvidia, as well as rivals Apple (AAPL), Intel (INTC), and AMD (AMD), are increasingly pushing the concept of running AI software in the home.
The thinking is pretty straightforward. Rather than having to use an online AI service, you can instead install an app on your computer, download an AI model of your choice, and get to work.
There are some pretty compelling reasons to run AI services on your own machine if you're so inclined. But it's also not for everyone.
When setting up your own AI system makes sense
Running AI locally means you can use AI apps and agents how you see fit without usage limits. You can also choose from a variety of open-weight models from numerous AI developers, such as Google, Meta, and Nvidia, or from Chinese model developers like Moonshot AI and Alibaba Cloud.
Unlike closed-weight models, like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra or Anthropic's Opus 5.5, open-weight models can be tuned to some extent. But the primary reason users download them is that they're largely free.
Local AI also provides better overall privacy, because your data stays on your machine rather than being sent up to the cloud, an important consideration for people working in fields such as law, medicine, or financial services.
More advanced users have also leaned into running AI on their systems to take advantage of AI agents like OpenClaw that can organize your email, launch and operate apps, and make purchases on your behalf.
The interest in agents sent early adopters scrambling for low-cost computers like Apple's Mac mini, which quickly became hard to come by in AI hotbeds like Silicon Valley.
More recently, AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots have introduced similar capabilities via cloud computing. But to take full advantage of those bots, you have to connect things like your Gmail, Uber, and other accounts to them, which means putting a lot of trust in Meta and OpenAI to protect your information.
When to stick to the cloud
While using your computer to run local AI models and agents provides improved privacy and enhanced customization options, doing so is a lot more complicated than simply logging into ChatGPT or Claude.

item.title: Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
2026-10-09
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/trump-disclosed-millions-in-new-trades-in-spacex-and-microsoft-today-he-gave-medals-to-their-ceos-182614694.html
Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
President Trump made over 500 securities trades in August in newly disclosed transactions valued at tens of millions of dollars, including in major tech companies whose leaders have become frequent guests at the White House.
According to a new ethics disclosure, Trump made at least 20 trades — a mix of purchases and sales worth millions of dollars — in Nvidia (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), SpaceX (SPCX), Alphabet (GOOG), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell (DELL), and Microsoft (MSFT).
The disclosure was released Thursday, the same day Trump appeared at a "New Golden Age Summit" in Washington, where he presented medals to the heads of those companies.
Trump gave the National Medal of Science to Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
"We have an extremely high-IQ audience," Trump said at the event as he lavished praise on the leaders and their companies, calling Elon Musk "a national treasure." Trump bought up to $5 million in SpaceX debt in August in the form of senior unsecured notes, the company's inaugural bond issuance, the disclosure shows.
"The entire world is running on Nvidia," Trump said of Jensen Huang and his company.
The new disclosure shows a continued high velocity of trading, particularly in tech stocks, in the president's account.
In total, Trump reported 517 transactions in August, a slower pace than previous months when the president's accounts often made over 1,000 transactions. Trump has disclosed more than 9,200 transactions so far in various documents over the first eight months of 2026.
Trump's brokerage accounts are managed by his company, the Trump Organization, which makes the trades and says they are overseen by third-party financial institutions without any input from Trump or his family.
"Neither President Trump, his family, nor The Trump Organization plays any role in selecting, directing, or approving specific investments," the Trump Organization said in a statement.
The largest disclosure in Thursday's release was a purchase of Meta (META) stock valued at between $5 million and $25 million.
The document also shows dozens of transactions valued at between $1 million and $5 million in major names including Microsoft, McDonald's (MCD), Comcast (CMCSA), ConocoPhillips (COP), and Abbott Labs (ABT.NE).
Trump sold between $1 million and $5 million worth of shares in Advanced Micro Devices, his only trade in that company in August.

In total, Trump reported 517 transactions in August, a slower pace than previous months when the president's accounts often made over 1,000 transactions. Trump has disclosed more than 9,200 transactions so far in various documents over the first eight months of 2026.

Trump's brokerage accounts are managed by his company, the Trump Organization, which makes the trades and says they are overseen by third-party financial institutions without any input from Trump or his family.

"Neither President Trump, his family, nor The Trump Organization plays any role in selecting, directing, or approving specific investments," the Trump Organization said in a statement.

The largest disclosure in Thursday's release was a purchase of Meta (META) stock valued at between $5 million and $25 million.

The document also shows dozens of transactions valued at between $1 million and $5 million in major names including Microsoft, McDonald's (MCD), Comcast (CMCSA), ConocoPhillips (COP), and Abbott Labs (ABT.NE).

Trump sold between $1 million and $5 million worth of shares in Advanced Micro Devices, his only trade in that company in August.

item.title: Boo
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Boo
2026-10-09
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/14-million-homes-will-change-hands-in-the-next-decade-as-boomers-age-170736414.html
Limited supply has been one factor stymying the US housing market. But some relief may be on the way as the population ages.
Baby boomers and the Silent Generation are expected to unload some 13.9 million homes in the next decade, 34% more than older households did in the past 10 years, according to Realtor.com calculations. Homeownership rates typically remain steady until owners reach their mid-70s, then begin to decline as older owners move in with family, enter care homes, or transition to rentals. This year, the oldest boomers turn 80.
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
The expected transfer of homes is sometimes called the "silver tsunami."
It's expected to help the US's housing shortage, although it won't fix it entirely. Most older homeowners have midsize or larger homes, meaning the new inventory that's expected to come to market won't be much help to first-time buyers targeting smaller starter homes, which are in particularly short supply.
But current homeowners looking to move into larger digs may be at an advantage. Some 9.9 million of the expected homes that will be released have three to four bedrooms, a popular size for families. If half of those homes hit the market, inventory would rise more than 12%, according to Realtor.com.
Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.author: Catherine Larkin
item.description:
Chipotle Jumps After Report That Starbucks Has Explored Takeover
2026-10-09
Por Catherine Larkin
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/chipotle-jumps-report-starbucks-explored-141555921.html
(Bloomberg) -- Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. (CMG) shares jumped after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks Corp. has worked with advisers in recent months on a takeover proposal for the burrito chain.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The status of the takeover plans couldn't be immediately learned and a mega deal of this size might never get off the ground, the Times said, citing people familiar with the matter. Brian Niccol, Starbucks' chief executive officer since 2024, previously was the top executive at Chipotle.
Shares of Chipotle surged as much as 8.6% in New York trading on Thursday. Starbucks declined as much as 6.7%, the most intraday in more than a year.

item.title: Trump administration freezes green cards for Microsoft
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Trump administration freezes green cards for Microsoft
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Trump administration freezes green cards for Microsoft, IT firms, probes universities.
By Akash Sriram and Steve Holland
WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - The US suspended Microsoft (MSFT.O), major IT outsourcers and software maker Adobe (ADBE.O), from a key green-card program on Thursday while opening probes into nine top universities, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American ‌jobs.
Since taking office, US President Donald Trump has pursued a broad effort to reduce the number of foreign-born people in the US and curtail their pathway to residence and citizenship. Thursday's twin actions mark the broadest strike yet against skilled-worker immigration programs — potentially cutting off a common path to permanent residency for foreign tech workers — while putting some of the country's top research universities on notice.
"There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vice President JD Vance said. He said the company laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 green cards.
His comments came hours before Trump honored tech billionaires for their contributions to America, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Nadella once ⁠held an H-1B visa, as did Elon Musk, who was also honored, while three of the other CEOs honored are immigrants.
Nadella thanked Trump for the medal, saying in a post on X he would continue to advance technology and drive American prosperity.
Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, or the permanent labor certification process, according to data from the US labor department. Under PERM, which most employment-based green cards require, employers must show a foreign hire will not hurt US workers' wages or jobs.
The company said in a statement that about 80% of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, not to hire new workers. In July, the company said it would cut 4,800 jobs, or about 2.1% of its global workforce.
CRACKDOWN WIDENS
Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said the suspension would also cover Cognizant (CTSH.O), Infosys (INFY.NS), Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS), Wipro (WIPR.NS), HCL Technologies (HCLT.NS), and Capgemini (CAPP.PA). "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said.
He said these companies had since 2009 sought almost three million foreign workers, and had received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications.
Amazon.com was the largest employer of approved H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal 2026, followed by Tata Consultancy ‌Services, Infosys, ⁠Apple and Microsoft, according to US immigration data.
Item 1 of 2 US Vice President JD Vance makes an H-1B fraud announcement during a press conference on anti-fraud initiatives in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House campus in Washington, D.C., US, October 8, 2026. REUTERS/Nathan Howard
US Vice President JD Vance makes an H-1B fraud announcement during a press conference on anti-fraud initiatives in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House campus in Washington, D.C., US, October 8, 2026. REUTERS/Nathan Howard Purchase Licensing Rights.
Vance said the suspensions would last "as long as it needs to," and that the administration wanted the companies to change how they hire. He said some companies post ineffective job ads, then point to the lack of applicants to justify hiring lower-paid foreign workers.
Microsoft said in its statement that it pays its H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work.
Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro and Capgemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tata Consultancy S
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Google Launches Workplace AI Agent That Acts Like Colleague
item.author: Davey Alba; Julia Love
item.description:
Google Launches Workplace AI Agent That Acts Like Colleague
2026-10-09
Por Davey Alba; Julia Love
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/google-launches-workplace-ai-agent-141743931.html
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google announced a Gemini agent for the workplace, ramping up competition with OpenAI, Anthropic PBC and Microsoft Corp. for corporate customers.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The artificial intelligence tool can be used for a range of tasks, from answering questions to content creation and coding, the company said on Thursday. The Gemini agent operates inside Google apps, including Gmail, Drive, Docs and Calendar, Google said.
Google's new agent is built to work like a colleague rather than a chatbot, with its own corporate identity and the ability to pursue a goal across several days, the company said. That goes beyond Google's previous agent offerings, which in many cases responded to prompts or ran preset tasks within a single app.
"It chooses the best model for the job, has built-in cost controls, and most importantly, has the security, administration and governance required by your company," Google Cloud Chief Executive Officer Thomas Kurian said in a blog post announcing the new agent.
The launch is aimed at winning business customers that Google needs to justify its hundreds of billions of dollars in AI infrastructure spending. The company is in a heated race with Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Amazon.com Inc. to monetize those investments through lucrative corporate contracts.
Some Google employees have expressed concerns that the company's capabilities at the cutting edge have fallen behind rivals, particularly in coding tasks. Google has begun sharing its next, improved flagship artificial intelligence model, Gemini 4 Argon, with trusted cybersecurity partners.
Alphabet shares were little changed in New York.
(Updated with more context starting in the third paragraph.)
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
item.author: Lucia Mutikani
item.description:
US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
2026-10-09
Por Lucia Mutikani
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-weekly-jobless-claims-fall-123611883.html
US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
1 / 13
US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
A "we're hiring" sign is displayed outside a Target store, after U.S. employment growth slowed more than expected in July, in Encinitas, California, U.S. August 1, 2025. REUTERS/Mike Blake
WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in September.
Weekly jobless claims have now remained near 57-year lows for four straight weeks, the report from the Labor Department showed on Thursday, amid historically low layoffs.
Though employers are hoarding workers against the backdrop of strong profit growth and stock market performance, they have remained hesitant to add to headcount, making it harder for those who lose their jobs to find new opportunities. Economists have blamed that trend on uncertainty, first from tariffs and then the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has pushed up diesel prices to record highs and boosted prices for other commodities.
"It's still a 'low-hire, low-fire' job market," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "That's great for anyone who has a job and wants to keep it, but it's tough for job seekers."
Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 2,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended October 3, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 200,000 claims for the latest week.
Claims have held below the 200,000 mark since the second week of September. California and Illinois were the only states to report an increase in unadjusted applications in excess of 1,000. The four-week moving average of claims, viewed as a better gauge of labor market trends as it irons out week-to-week volatility, fell 2,500 to 198,000 last week, the lowest level since early October 2022.
Stocks on Wall Street were trading lower. The dollar slipped against a basket of currencies.
TEPID JOB GROWTH
Nonfarm payrolls increased by a paltry 29,000 jobs in September, the government reported last week. Economists say tepid hiring and a shrinking labor pool amid retirements and an immigration crackdown are holding back job growth, leaving low layoffs to anchor the labor market.
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 policy meeting, published on Wednesday, showed officials "judged that labor market conditions were stable and generally viewed the labor market as close to maximum employment." The minutes also noted that policymakers "generally viewed the upside and downside risks to the labor market as broadly balanced."
The US central bank last month raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead.
The odds of another rate hike this month were diminished by the underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected inflation readings for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 17,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.716 million during the week ended September 26. item.content:encoded:
US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week

2026-10-09

Por Lucia Mutikani

https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-weekly-jobless-claims-fall-123611883.html

US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week

1 / 13

US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week

A "we're hiring" sign is displayed outside a Target store, after U.S. employment growth slowed more than expected in July, in Encinitas, California, U.S. August 1, 2025. REUTERS/Mike Blake

WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) - The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in September.

Weekly jobless claims have now remained near 57-year lows for four straight weeks, the report from the Labor Department showed on Thursday, amid historically low layoffs.

Though employers are hoarding workers against the backdrop of strong profit growth and stock market performance, they have remained hesitant to add to headcount, making it harder for those who lose their jobs to find new opportunities. Economists have blamed that trend on uncertainty, first from tariffs and then the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has pushed up diesel prices to record highs and boosted prices for other commodities.

"It's still a 'low-hire, low-fire' job market," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "That's great for anyone who has a job and wants to keep it, but it's tough for job seekers."

Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 2,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended October 3, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 200,000 claims for the latest week.

Claims have held below the 200,000 mark since the second week of September. California and Illinois were the only states to report an increase in unadjusted applications in excess of 1,000. The four-week moving average of claims, viewed as a better gauge of labor market trends as it irons out week-to-week volatility, fell 2,500 to 198,000 last week, the lowest level since early October 2022.

Stocks on Wall Street were trading lower. The dollar slipped against a basket of currencies.

TEPID JOB GROWTH

Nonfarm payrolls increased by a paltry 29,000 jobs in September, the government reported last week. Economists say tepid hiring and a shrinking labor pool amid retirements and an immigration crackdown are holding back job growth, leaving low layoffs to anchor the labor market.

Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 policy meeting, published on Wednesday, showed officials "judged that labor market conditions were stable and generally viewed the labor market as close to maximum employment." The minutes also noted that policymakers "generally viewed the upside and downside risks to the labor market as broadly balanced."

The US central bank last month raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead.

The odds of another rate hike this month were diminished by the underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected inflation readings for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December.

The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 17,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.716 million during the week ended September 26. The so-called continued claims had dropped to a 3-1/2-year low in the prior week.

Some economists argued that the still-low level of continued claims was masking a gradual labor market weakening as a group of unemployed people, including recent college graduates, were ineligible for benefits because of limited or no work history.

Some long-term unemployed people may have exhausted their eligibility

item.title: Apple is the 'toll collector on the consumer AI highway,' Dan Ives says
item.author: Ethan Wolff-Mann
item.description:
Apple is the 'toll collector on the consumer AI highway,' Dan Ives says
2026-10-09
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/apple-is-the-toll-collector-on-the-consumer-ai-highway-dan-ives-says-100000129.html
Apple (AAPL) has positioned itself many times between the consumer and what they want, with great success.
The iTunes store. The App store. As Michael Gambon said in "Layer Cake" — a quote I have written about before and will many times again — "The art of good business is being a good middleman," and Apple understands this as well as anyone.
But Apple's ability to execute this strategy is thanks to its access to that middle ground: Controlling and supplying the world's most popular devices, like the iPhone and iPad, makes this possible.
Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives said this sums up his bullish case for the slick hardware king, the sometimes-most-valuable company, still flying high without being directly involved in frontier AI.
"In our view, Apple will be the toll collector on the consumer AI highway," Ives wrote in a note to clients on Thursday. "While the last few years Apple has struggled with its AI strategy and went through many twists and turns, now finally Ternus and Cupertino have a horse in the race with an AI vision that will build over the coming years into a formidable piece of the Apple strategy."
In Ives's view, letting the other companies develop — and pay for — the AI savoir faire should work out just fine, given that everyone will have to go through that corporate tollbooth, similar to how app developers had to go through and tithe Cupertino its standard 30% commission.
Ives said this is underappreciated and not priced into Apple's stock, and he believes another $75 should be tacked onto the company's share price, as AI capabilities will facilitate upgrades and a 15% boost in services revenue.
If this happens, it'll be an impressive Houdini from what seemed to be an intractable position of being left in the dust by its tech peers. And it'll show how reach and network effects were just as important as technological innovation.
"Much of the debate has centered on whether Apple arrived early or late to generative AI," Ives wrote. "We think the question that matters more is how well the company can put useful AI in front of an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices and 1.5 billion iPhones."
If the company could put U2 into everyone's pocket (without asking), it's not to be underestimated.
Ethan Wolff-Mann is a Senior Editor at Yahoo Finance, running newsletters. Follow him on X @ewolffmann.

item.title: Bubble warnings are spiking. But bullish retail investors are buying the high.
item.author: Ethan Wolff-Mann
item.description:
Bubble warnings are spiking. But bullish retail investors are buying the high.
2026-10-09
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bubble-warnings-are-spiking-but-bullish-retail-investors-are-buying-the-high-100000102.html
Hedge fund legend Ray Dalio of Bridgewater Associates became the latest big name to issue a warning about a potential AI bubble, noting that the market is "close to that" level.
On top of that, Dalio gave investors something actually specific to watch: when billionaires decide to take profits and sell.
While Dalio was speaking generally about market concentration, hype, and the vibe-based phenomena associated with bubbles, others have been a little more specific.
Joachim Klement, a head market strategist at UK investment bank Panmure Liberum, told Bloomberg that his "core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028," as he adjusted his outlook.
While Klement, who was at UBS for years, has a view that's heterodox compared to his Wall Street peers, this big proclamation hit harder given his September projection for the S&P 500 for year-end 2027 was a bullish 8,300.
It's 5,000 now, with Klement making the case that a market derailing could come from high debt and inflation torpedoing hyperscaler free cash flow and causing an AI implosion.
The market can — and will — debate the merits of Klement's arguments over the coming months as the resilience of the economy and market gets tested. But one thing is clear: Retail investors are completely unbothered.
According to Bank of America, regular people (and hedge funds) are actually feeling bullish.
"Retail clients were net buyers — the first inflows from retail since late July," BofA Securities Jill Carey Hall wrote in a Wednesday note to clients.
We can see a similar trend, albeit less scientifically, by looking at Google Trends to see whether people are searching for "stock market bubble." A fast but loose market anxiety shortcut, to be sure, but even Wall Street uses it sometimes.
Looking at the past year, we see an early June high of "100" — these are relatively dimensionless numbers — and a downward trend for the most part since then, with a jump in September and a drop into Thursday's "14."
It's clear we're nowhere near other, more fraught moments of 2026. But that doesn't mean Dalio and Klement are wrong. And for what it's worth, the Google Trends prediction line is trending up. Perhaps this Bloomberg headline sums up the moment, or possibly the entire cycle, like no other: "Novogratz joins crowd warning of AI bubble, says pile in anyway."
Ethan Wolff-Mann is a Senior Editor at Yahoo Finance, running newsletters. Follow him on X @ewolffmann.

item.title: Goldman’s stock edges towards 2026 flatline ahead of earnings
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
Goldman’s stock edges towards 2026 flatline ahead of earnings
2026-10-09
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/goldman-sachs-stock-loses-nearly-all-year-to-date-gains-as-bond-yields-rise-141150928.html
Goldman Sachs (GS) stock edged lower on Thursday, extending a painful sell-off that has almost zeroed out 2026 gains for the storied Wall Street bank days ahead of its third quarter earnings release.
Goldman's stock has fallen in 10 of the past 12 weeks, according to Yahoo Finance data, marking a drop of more than 20% since its July peak. For the year, shares were up 0.23% as of Thursday's close.
The retreat comes as a dramatic reversal of investor appetite.
The storied investment bank stood at the center of a banner first half for Wall Street, powered by unusually active markets and a wave of mega corporate deals.
First-half profits have already blown past New York State's full-year forecast, with bonuses now projected to hit another yearly high. Compensation boutique Johnson Associates anticipates the same boom, with big banks leading.
Goldman's extraordinary run over the past five years is also about to deliver a massive payday for its top executives. Some 20 Goldman Sachs executives are set to receive more than $500 million in special equity awards later this month, according to a Bloomberg report. CEO David Solomon alone stands to receive more than $100 million.
The awards, granted five years ago and tied to Goldman's performance over that period, underscore the contrast between the fortunes Wall Street's top bankers have enjoyed and the more uncertain outlook investors now see for the industry.
A sharp rise in government bond yields has raised borrowing costs, threatening to complicate deals and cool demand for financing. The trading boom is also showing signs of fatigue as the global bond market rout has deepened.
Goldman's fixed income, currencies, and commodities trading and financing operations "have been a little bit softer on a relative basis," CEO David Solomon said at a September Barclays conference in New York.
Announced mergers and acquisitions deals globally also slowed sharply during the third quarter, raising questions about whether this year's investment banking surge can keep up momentum into next year.
The stock pressure extends well beyond Goldman Sachs. US bank stocks broadly have retreated in recent weeks as investors reassess the economic outlook amid a new era of interest rate hikes.
Investors will get a detailed look at how Goldman Sachs and other big banks are faring early next week as third quarter bank earnings begin on Tuesday.
David Hollerith covers a range of developments throughout the financial sector, from Wall Street to banking and asset management to crypto and fintech. Email him at david.hollerith@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on X at @DsHollers.

item.title: Fed’s Waller sees additional rate hikes to get inflation down faster
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed’s Waller sees additional rate hikes to get inflation down faster
2026-10-09
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/feds-waller-sees-additional-rate-hikes-to-get-inflation-down-faster-083000282.html
Federal Reserve Governor Chris Waller said in a speech Thursday that he expects the Fed will need to enact more interest rate hikes to bring down inflation faster if economic data comes in as he expects.
"If the economic data continue to come in as expected, I anticipate additional hikes to support a timelier return of inflation to our 2% goal," Waller said at the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye İstanbul Economic Forum. "But there is some flexibility about when those hikes will occur. The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, but they should be in place in an acceptable period of time."
Waller noted that a convergence of factors has gelled into persistent inflationary forces, including hopes for a quick ending to the Middle East conflict and warnings that low inventories and damaged infrastructure could keep oil prices high through 2027. He also pointed out that the artificial intelligence build-out has significantly driven up high-tech consumer prices, and projections of its size have ballooned. Additionally, he said, continuing trade conflicts threaten new tariffs that could put upward pressure on inflation yet again.
"When the first inflation reading for August came in hot just before the FOMC's September meeting, it was impossible to deny that inflation was still too high and not making sufficient progress toward our target," Waller said.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
Waller sees economic activity strengthening in the second half of this year, and says he's "not greatly concerned" that higher interest rates threaten to markedly slow down the economy.
"But I am concerned that the recent acceleration in inflation — after what soon will be five and a half years of it above the FOMC's target — will lead consumers, investors, and price-setting businesses to revise up their expectations for future inflation."
He noted that he sees the economy in roughly the same place as it was at the time of the Fed's policy meeting in mid-September.
"Overall, the new data reinforce my view that the labor market is stable and inflation is too high," he said. "For at least the near term, policy will be focused on the inflation side of our mandate."
Waller also made a point of sharing how he believes the Fed should communicate its interest rate expectations. He doesn't think choosing to say nothing or offering a strong indication of what the Fed will do is how the central bank should communicate. Rather, he believes an in-between approach of signaling the amount of rate hikes over some time interval, while not saying what the pace of hikes will be or how large they will be, would offer flexibility, while keeping the public informed.

item.title: Rapid bond yield moves have preceded nearly every major financial blowup: Chart of the Day
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Rapid bond yield moves have preceded nearly every major financial blowup: Chart of the Day
2026-10-09
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/rapid-bond-yield-moves-have-preceded-nearly-every-major-financial-blowup-chart-of-the-day-150720851.html
The risk around rising bond yields isn't just higher borrowing costs. It's what happens when yields move too far too fast.
Macquarie strategists pointed out that "almost all of the high-profile financial blow-outs" over the past five decades have occurred in the immediate aftermath of rapid moves in bond yields.
"That is, in the past 50 years, sharp increases (or sharp decreases) in long-term yields have taken place every few years, and when they have taken place, another financial company, or heavy borrower has imploded," Macquarie global strategists Thierry Wizman and Gareth Berry wrote on Wednesday.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
Macquarie research points to "balance sheet-induced mini-crises" following rapid yield moves, ranging from the collapse of Franklin National Bank in 1974 to the municipal bankruptcy of Orange County in 1994 and, most recently, the implosion of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023.
The $200 billion institution collapsed in less than 48 hours after Federal Reserve interest rate hikes eroded the value of the bank's long-term bond portfolio.
The blowout in Treasury yields, which move inversely with bond prices, has been happening worldwide.
As the 10-year Treasury (^TNX) recently climbed to its highest level since 2002, France, Italy, Indonesia, Japan, and South Korea have also seen their benchmark yields rise at least 100 basis points since the start of the year, according to Yardeni Research data.
Macquarie strategists argue that there is a "direct and self-reinforcing causal connection" between recent street riots over proposed budget cuts in France and the European country's bond market stress.
Even as bond yields revert to their levels prior to the 2008 financial crisis, strong earnings coupled with a pause in interest rate hikes from the Fed, are expected to keep the stock market grinding higher.
That doesn't mean Wall Street strategists aren't watching for a critical threshold in the 10-year yield.
"Historical data show that valuations start compressing after 5.5%, and everyone from investors to corporations to consumers would have to redo the math on their investments," Fundstrat economic strategist Hardika Singh recently noted.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

item.title: OpenAI's annualized revenue $20 billion lower than prior investor estimates
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
OpenAI's annualized revenue $20 billion lower than prior investor estimates
2026-10-09
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/openais-annualized-revenue-20-billion-lower-than-prior-investor-estimates-174058048.html
OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) annualized revenue is reportedly $20 billion short of prior estimates.
According to the Financial Times, the AI startup's annualized revenue topped out at roughly $50 billion as of September, well below the $70 billion outlets previously estimated.
The dramatic swing is a result of investor miscalculations. The FT said investors who initially cited the $70 billion figure arrived at the number by comparing OpenAI's revenue with Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT).
Annualized revenue takes a snapshot of revenue for a certain period and extrapolates it across a year. But OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently.
Investors initially tried to determine whether OpenAI's sales reached $40 billion in August. Later, when OpenAI told investors that revenue grew 70%, they added that amount to the initial $40 billion estimate and landed on $70 billion.
At $50 billion, OpenAI's annualized revenue would now fall below Anthropic's $65 billion in annualized sales.
OpenAI is widely anticipated to kick off its initial public offering sometime in early 2027, while Anthropic is rumored to hit the public market sometime before Thanksgiving, with its public S-1 investor prospectus expected to land any day now.
Both companies are battling for enterprise customers, offering up products including coding and general-purpose AI agents.
Last week, OpenAI held its annual developers conference, where it debuted its new Dots AI agents for enterprise workers and its latest model, GPT-6.1 Sol.

item.title: Oil falls to $103 as Trump says US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Oil falls to $103 as Trump says US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections
2026-10-09
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-falls-to-103-as-trump-says-us-will-not-attack-iran-before-the-midterm-elections-171630147.html
Oil prices trimmed gains on Thursday after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
Brent crude (BZ=F) fell to $103 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) dropped to $90 a barrel.
The move came after Trump posted on social media, "We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran."
He went on to say that "we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd."
The president's post came after The Atlantic reported that the Trump administration was considering striking Iran before the midterm elections. The outlet said the Pentagon is weighing options, though no final decision has been made.
Oil rose this week amid increased incidents of vessel attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi-claimed attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia.
Meanwhile, Hurricane Isaias is nearing the Gulf Coast, threatening to make landfall on Friday. Chevron (CVX) said it is evacuating nonessential personnel from its offshore platforms in the region.
"These factors outweighed the news that the International Energy Agency was accelerating the release of stockpiles of oil and distillates," noted David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, on Thursday.
Higher energy costs are adding to expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain its tightening stance to curb inflation. The market fully priced in a 25 basis point Federal Reserve rate increase in December.
Bond yields have climbed higher worldwide, with the 10-year yield (^TNX) rising to 5.32%.
Volatile crude oil costs, along with maxed-out refining capacity, have caused refined fuel prices to surge.
Gasoline prices averaged $4.36 per gallon on Thursday, per AAA data. Diesel prices stood at $6.28 per gallon, down $0.02 from Wednesday.
The administration has been looking for ways to ease high energy costs ahead of November's midterm elections.
On Tuesday, President Trump, responding to a reporter, said he is considering suspending the federal gas tax.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: ‘A lot of sticker shock’: Home heating costs surge for millions amid oil crisis
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
‘A lot of sticker shock’: Home heating costs surge for millions amid oil crisis
2026-10-09
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/a-lot-of-sticker-shock-home-heating-costs-soar-for-millions-amid-oil-crisis-160853971.html
The ongoing global energy crunch doesn't just cause pain at the gas pump: As winter approaches, millions of Americans are facing dramatic spikes in their home heating costs.
The price of heating oil, which some 4.8 million households, mostly in the Northeast and Alaska, use to heat their homes, is approaching all-time highs as two wars strain global supply.
Heating oil costs are expected to jump 50% this winter, according to one estimate from the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, adding nearly $900 to the average home's heating bill. The jump is catching consumers by surprise at a time of year when many households fill their tanks for winter, and it's stoking concern that the high prices will force low-income families to make tough choices between warming their homes and paying for necessities.
"There's a lot of sticker shock," said Chris Herb, president of the Connecticut Energy Marketers Association, a trade group for local fuel providers and other energy companies in the state.
Heating oil is nearly identical to diesel, and diesel prices have continued to rise while crude oil prices have plateaued as higher seasonal demand collides with ongoing supply shocks. The Iran War has disrupted exporters' ability to reliably pass through the Strait of Hormuz, while escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries have limited another key source of supply.
In recent weeks, diesel prices have topped $6.50 a gallon, breaking an all-time record. And across the Northeastern states, heating oil prices have either recently broken or are just short of the highest levels on record.
"Diesel and heating oil are basically directly tied now," said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy. "Diesel setting all-time records is certainly very worrisome for home heating oil expenses this winter."
A gallon of heating oil now averages around $5.96 in Maine, where more than half the state relies on oil, the highest share anywhere in the country. Prices are $5.87 in Vermont and $5.91 in Connecticut, meaning 100 gallons, a common minimum order threshold, comes out to nearly $600.
During the winter months, a typical home relying on heating oil alone can run through 100 gallons in a few weeks.
Homeowners have been making tough choices: Fill up now, or hold off in hopes that prices fall in the months ahead? Look into alternative heating sources that might be pricey up front but deliver savings in the long-term? Lower the thermostat and shiver to stretch a tank's worth of oil longer?
'Do I order? Do I hold off?'
In Connecticut, Herb said suppliers were seeing more business than is typical for September, perhaps a sign that households who had been waiting in vain for prices to go down after February's Iran war shock didn't want to risk another price jump later in the season.

item.content:encoded:
‘A lot of sticker shock’: Home heating costs surge for millions amid oil crisis

2026-10-09

Por Claire Boston

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/a-lot-of-sticker-shock-home-heating-costs-soar-for-millions-amid-oil-crisis-160853971.html

The ongoing global energy crunch doesn't just cause pain at the gas pump: As winter approaches, millions of Americans are facing dramatic spikes in their home heating costs.

The price of heating oil, which some 4.8 million households, mostly in the Northeast and Alaska, use to heat their homes, is approaching all-time highs as two wars strain global supply.

Heating oil costs are expected to jump 50% this winter, according to one estimate from the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, adding nearly $900 to the average home's heating bill. The jump is catching consumers by surprise at a time of year when many households fill their tanks for winter, and it's stoking concern that the high prices will force low-income families to make tough choices between warming their homes and paying for necessities.

"There's a lot of sticker shock," said Chris Herb, president of the Connecticut Energy Marketers Association, a trade group for local fuel providers and other energy companies in the state.

Heating oil is nearly identical to diesel, and diesel prices have continued to rise while crude oil prices have plateaued as higher seasonal demand collides with ongoing supply shocks. The Iran War has disrupted exporters' ability to reliably pass through the Strait of Hormuz, while escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries have limited another key source of supply.

In recent weeks, diesel prices have topped $6.50 a gallon, breaking an all-time record. And across the Northeastern states, heating oil prices have either recently broken or are just short of the highest levels on record.

"Diesel and heating oil are basically directly tied now," said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy. "Diesel setting all-time records is certainly very worrisome for home heating oil expenses this winter."

A gallon of heating oil now averages around $5.96 in Maine, where more than half the state relies on oil, the highest share anywhere in the country. Prices are $5.87 in Vermont and $5.91 in Connecticut, meaning 100 gallons, a common minimum order threshold, comes out to nearly $600.

During the winter months, a typical home relying on heating oil alone can run through 100 gallons in a few weeks.

Homeowners have been making tough choices: Fill up now, or hold off in hopes that prices fall in the months ahead? Look into alternative heating sources that might be pricey up front but deliver savings in the long-term? Lower the thermostat and shiver to stretch a tank's worth of oil longer?

'Do I order? Do I hold off?'

In Connecticut, Herb said suppliers were seeing more business than is typical for September, perhaps a sign that households who had been waiting in vain for prices to go down after February's Iran war shock didn't want to risk another price jump later in the season.

"That's when I started thinking, 'Do I order? Do I hold off?'" she said. "I really didn't think it would get this bad."

item.title: SpaceX stock slips on report of its $40 billion in new debt for Nvidia chips
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
SpaceX stock slips on report of its $40 billion in new debt for Nvidia chips
2026-10-09
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-stock-slips-on-report-of-its-40-billion-in-new-debt-for-nvidia-chips-140223011.html
SpaceX (SPCX) stock slipped on Wednesday as the Elon Musk-led space and AI company is reportedly set to tap the debt markets in a big way.
Bloomberg reported that SpaceX is looking to issue $40 billion in new debt to buy Nvidia chips for its data centers. Per the report, the split would be $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt, with bond investment giant PIMCO looking at the deal, and Apollo Global leading the financing. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
SpaceX stock closed down 2.5%.
The data center business has been good for SpaceX. The company's data centers in Memphis, Tenn., dubbed Colossus 1 and 2, are generating billions per month in recurring revenue from AI compute services.
Last month, SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen updated investors on the size of the company's AI compute business.
"We're on track, or we believe we're on track, to hit $100 billion ARR," Johnsen said about SpaceX's overall annual recurring revenue target, as AI compute deals helped fuel the growth. "What I would tell you, an update to that is that just earlier this month we closed another hosting deal, and that translates into about $1.11 billion a month starting December 1st of this year, which is another roughly $13 billion of ARR."
It's a big feather in SpaceX's cap, which traditionally relied on rocket launches and Starlink internet service as its main revenue drivers.
Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives, a notable SpaceX bull on Wall Street, said the deal provided "firepower for [SpaceX's] AI buildout," even if the debt picture is growing.
"The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage. We think the contracted backlog in AI and the cash generation of Starlink give SpaceX the capacity to service it, and we would rather see this compute financed and deployed than deferred," Ives said in a note published Wednesday morning.
Ives has an Outperform rating on SpaceX and a $225 price target.
Earlier this week, Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas wrote that SpaceX stock was "cheap" and that now is the time to buy ahead of the upcoming Starship 15 launch, likely scheduled for late October or November.

item.title: Crocs used to be wildly exposed to oil prices. Not anymore.
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Crocs used to be wildly exposed to oil prices. Not anymore.
2026-10-09
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/crocs-used-to-be-wildly-exposed-to-oil-prices-not-anymore-100000788.html
When you're talking about Crocs (CROX) on the internet, you're usually talking about nurses, a fashion faux pas, some Gen Z trend incomprehensible to the over-28 crowd, or whether the wearer was in sport mode.
You typically don't think of oil.
But this is the other side of the petrochemical business — it's not just about diesel and gas tanks. While a lot of companies are exposed to oil volatility because of shipping costs, Crocs has traditionally seen additional exposure because of the raw materials it uses to construct its footwear.
Croslite, the signature foam its clogs are made of, accounts for more than 80% of the materials used across Crocs product lines, according to the company. Since Croslite is derived largely from oil, the company is doubly vulnerable to the rising costs of crude (CL=F, BZ=F).
Read more: How the Iran war drives up the cost of gas and groceries
But despite that exposure, it seems Crocs has been able to tame one of the wildest manufacturing input costs, yet again.
According to Bank of America analysts led by Kendall Toscano, Crocs is likely to conquer 2027 without much trouble, following 2022, when it similarly navigated an oil shock. The shoemaker hasn't raised prices on its Classic Clog since 2021.
Specifically, Toscano et al. say the pressure of fuel surcharges and materials in 2027 ("assuming no moderation") will be offset by the company's "innovation."
"Innovation?" You might be thinking.
Yes. Crocs' exposure to oil has served as a positive catalyst for the company by turning its shift away from petrochemicals into a sustainability story — and critically doing so before the Hormuz crisis.
Starting in 2024, the company achieved a milestone by producing Croslite with 25% bio-circular content, or plant-based waste. By 2030, the company aims to achieve a Croslite formulation that's 50% bio-based — meaningful shifts away from oil and its fickle fluctuations.
And as a nice sustainability story, the company points out that by increasing the bio-circular content in its Croslite compounds, Crocs has reduced the Classic Clog's carbon footprint by 10% compared to the 2021 baseline.
That's, no doubt, compelling marketing material. But it has also helped shield the company from the oil shocks of the Iran war — and whatever else is to come.
Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban.
