item.title: Oil prices climb above $100 on Strait of Hormuz attacks, Gulf storm threat
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Oil prices climb above $100 on Strait of Hormuz attacks, Gulf storm threat
2026-10-09
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-prices-climb-above-100-on-strait-of-hormuz-attacks-gulf-storm-threat-122612488.html
Oil prices rose on Wednesday amid increased attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and an incoming storm in the Gulf Coast region.
Brent crude (BZ=F) rose to trade back above $101 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) was close to $90 a barrel.
Despite increased shipments through the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks, UK officials have reported at least nine attacks in the critical waterway so far in October amid a continued US-Iran conflict.
Meanwhile, a tropical storm is nearing the Gulf coast, threatening to make landfall as a hurricane by Friday. Chevron said it is evacuating nonessential personnel from its offshore platforms in the region.
Volatile crude oil costs, along with maxed-out refining capacity, have caused refined fuel prices to surge.
Gasoline prices averaged $4.36 per gallon on Wednesday, compared to $3.12 a year ago. Diesel prices stood at $6.30 per gallon.
On Tuesday, President Trump, responding to a reporter, said he is considering suspending the federal gas tax.
The administration has been looking for ways to ease high energy costs ahead of November's mid-term elections.
"Well, we're thinking about that," Trump replied when asked if the tax would be suspended.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Venture capital funding just blew past 2025 by 53% — here's why that's good for you
item.author: Ethan Wolff-Mann
item.description:
Venture capital funding just blew past 2025 by 53% — here's why that's good for you
2026-10-09
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/venture-capital-funding-just-blew-past-2025-by-53--heres-why-thats-good-for-you-100000412.html
For some investors, the S&P 500 (^GSPC) in the 7,800s merits a pat on the back. Congratulations to you for sticking it out through a litany of crises and for staying invested and focused on the long run.
And, most importantly, you might think, for putting money into the stock market a long time ago.
Perhaps. That's the first part of the old adage about trees: "The best time to plant a tree is decades ago."
But the punchline, "the second-best time is right now," also applies to the stock market — and DataTrek's Jessica Rabe has the receipts.
Investing into an all-time high takes a lot of guts, as you and your money are quite literally venturing into the unknown, and there's always a part of every investor who can't help but wonder if "this time is different," especially given the stock market's concentration. Not just the winners and losers, but the entire arc of the US economy. Perhaps one thinks of Rome.
But Rabe offered comfort for this thinking that goes beyond "stocks usually go up over time," though we'll take the opportunity to note that they do.
Global venture capital funding so far this year, Rabe noted, has already blown by 2025's levels by 53% in the first three quarters, according to Crunchbase. Good for the rich accredited investors who can get in early, sure. But also good for literally everyone who has hopes for S&P 10,000.
"Venture capital effectively serves as a free R&D engine for stock investors," Rabe wrote. "VCs do the hard work of identifying, funding, nurturing, and scaling thousands of potentially disruptive companies."

item.title: The Fed was unanimous about raising rates in September. Economic signals have since changed.
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
The Fed was unanimous about raising rates in September. Economic signals have since changed.
2026-10-09
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/the-fed-was-unanimous-about-raising-rates-in-september-economic-signals-have-since-changed-184839972.html
Minutes from the Federal Reserve's September policy meeting reflect unanimous agreement among officials that interest rates needed to be higher to combat persistent inflation.
"Participants generally emphasized that inflation remained elevated while the labor market appeared to be near full employment, with some signs of strengthening, and that economic activity was expanding at a solid pace. Furthermore, almost all participants assessed that, while inflation risks were tilted to the upside, risks to the labor market had diminished and were now broadly balanced," minutes from the Sept. 16 meeting released Wednesday stated.
"Based on the outlook and the changing balance of risks, all participants viewed a higher target range for the federal funds rate as appropriate."
The Fed voted unanimously on Sept. 16 to raise rates, the first hike in three years. And at the time, most Federal Open Market Committee members saw a need for at least one more 25 basis point rate hike this year.
Markets were banking on a hike and expecting more to come.
But economic data released in the past few weeks has changed the picture considerably. "Core" PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, rose a relatively cool 3% in August, beating expectations for a rise of 3.3% and marking a drop from 3.3% in July. Meanwhile, September jobs numbers fell far short of economists' expectations, with a gain of just 29,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
That less rosy jobs picture, combined with a more positive read on inflation, had analysts — and some Fed officials — throwing cold water on the notion of another rate hike this month.
"This data won't shift the broader decision-making calculus for the Fed as inflation remains the supreme concern," Chris Hodge, chief economist for Natixis, previously told Yahoo Finance. "But with wages lower and the jobs picture a bit less rosy, it certainly decreases the urgency to hike in October (and perhaps December if inflation data cooperates)."
Even before the September job report, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed president John Williams had already begun to temper expectations for a rate hike later this month. Both struck a more cautious tone than several of their colleagues, acknowledging that inflation has remained too high, but that the central bank should take time to assess whether it's on a downward path.
Williams said that, after raising rates in September, he sees "no need for urgency" and that "we have time to gather more information."

item.title: Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
2026-10-07
Por Texto propio
Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war
Jacob Bogage · October 6, 2026
FAIRBANKS, Alaska, Oct 6 (Reuters) - US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how ‌Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
Vance, a longtime skeptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections.
Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns.
"If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel? And if you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched ⁠fuel. That's a very basic threshold issue," Vance said.
"I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity."
Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.
Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.
"We're not going to trade words for actions," Vance said.
UNCLEAR HOW IRAN MAKES DECISIONS: VANCE
Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.
Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
"One of the things we picked up on is it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions," Vance said. Separately, Trump said on Tuesday his " biggest problem " is no one knows who is running Iran.
Iran's ‌Foreign Ministry ⁠spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works.
"The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.
Vance told Reuters he has held personal conversations with field commanders to gauge battlefield conditions. He dismissed concerns over critical munitions shortages and added that while Iranian troops are periodically able to strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, they are largely unable to prevent energy exports through the waterway.
Vance declined to say if he was leading peace talks, though he is ⁠frequently cited as the White House's top negotiator.
"We're certainly involved," he said. "Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things."
The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress.
Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling voters they should not ⁠let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month's elections.
In Alaska, Vance rallied for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sharpens warning about a corporate credit squeeze: 'The market will ask for more'
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sharpens warning about a corporate credit squeeze: 'The market will ask for more'
2026-10-07
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jpmorgan-ceo-jamie-dimon-sharpens-warning-about-a-corporate-credit-squeeze-the-market-will-ask-for-more-151359247.html
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sharpens warning about a corporate credit squeeze: 'The market will ask for more'
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) CEO Jamie Dimon sharpened his warning about the risks of a global bond sell-off on Tuesday, saying the world's massive competition for capital could begin squeezing corporate borrowers.
Dimon warned that the combination of rising government borrowing costs and spending on the AI boom could spill into corporate credit markets, pushing up the costs for companies to refinance or raise new debt.
"There will be a point where the market will ask for more and more and more, and yeah, at one point that'll feed into corporate debt, corporate credit spreads, and things like that, which is how it normally happens," Dimon said in a Bloomberg interview on the sidelines of a JPMorgan event in London.
"The best thing to do with any of these things is deal with it before it becomes a crisis. If it becomes a crisis, we will deal with it. It just will be in a much less pleasant way," he added.
The warning comes as a global rout in bonds has pushed longer-term borrowing costs sharply higher in recent weeks, with the benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield recently surpassing heights not seen since 2002.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
That sell-off follows the start of the war in Iran, which has driven inflation materially higher. The US economy's strength, amid those price pressures, along with the AI boom's enormous new demand for capital, has exacerbated the dynamic.
Credit markets have already begun to show signs of stress as interest rates have moved higher. In recent weeks, the spread for insuring US junk bonds has widened significantly in the credit default swap market, according to LSEG data compiled by Yardeni Research.
Last week, JPMorgan strategists flagged leveraged loans in deeply distressed territory or those trading below 60 cents on the dollar, rose to $65 billion from a year ago to their highest level since March 2020.
Dimon has been delivering versions of this argument for months. In JPMorgan's April shareholder letter, he warned that the combination of spending on AI, defense, and infrastructure, along with large government deficits, should keep upward pressure on borrowing costs.
Weeks ago, he told Yahoo Finance, shortly after the Federal Reserve's September rate hike, that while he believed borrowing costs could continue to rise, the labor market's relative strength signaled that those costs hadn't yet translated into broader economic stress.
On Tuesday, Dimon focused on how those risks could play out for companies.

"There will be a point where the market will ask for more and more and more, and yeah, at one point that'll feed into corporate debt, corporate credit spreads, and things like that, which is how it normally happens," Dimon said in a Bloomberg interview on the sidelines of a JPMorgan event in London.
"The best thing to do with any of these things is deal with it before it becomes a crisis. If it becomes a crisis, we will deal with it. It just will be in a much less pleasant way," he added.
The warning comes as a global rout in bonds has pushed longer-term borrowing costs sharply higher in recent weeks, with the benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield recently surpassing heights not seen since 2002.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
That sell-off follows the start of the war in Iran, which has driven inflation materially higher. The US economy's strength, amid those price pressures, along with the AI boom's enormous new demand for capital, has exacerbated the dynamic.
Credit markets have already begun to show signs of stress as interest rates have moved higher. In recent weeks, the spread for insuring US junk bonds has widened significantly in the credit default swap market, according to LSEG data compiled by Yardeni Research.
Last week, JPMorgan strategists flagged leveraged loans in deeply distressed territory or those trading below 60 cents on the dollar, rose to $65 billion from a year ago to their highest level since March 2020.
Dimon has been delivering versions of this argument for months. In JPMorgan's April shareholder letter, he warned that the combination of spending on AI, defense, and infrastructure, along with large government deficits, should keep upward pressure on borrowing costs.
Weeks ago, he told Yahoo Finance, shortly after the Federal Reserve's September rate hike, that while he believed borrowing costs could continue to rise, the labor market's relative strength signaled that those costs hadn't yet translated into broader economic stress.
On Tuesday, Dimon focused on how those risks could play out for companies.

item.title: Google signs 20-year nuclear deal with Constellation Energy to power AI build-out
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Google signs 20-year nuclear deal with Constellation Energy to power AI build-out
2026-10-07
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/google-signs-20-year-nuclear-deal-with-constellation-energy-to-power-ai-build-out-131104702.html
Google (GOOG, GOOGL) on Tuesday said it has inked a $4.3 billion deal with Constellation Energy (CEG) to bring 890 megawatts of nuclear energy online via a 20-year power purchasing agreement.
Constellation Energy stock climbed more than 12% on the news. Google parent Alphabet stock was flat.
The new capacity, the company said, will come from upgrades at six existing nuclear plants in Illinois, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania, and will include improvements such as modernized turbines, steam generators, and digital control systems.
The tech giant said the agreement provides Constellation with the revenue certainty needed to invest in updates to 11 of its reactors while ensuring customers don't incur additional costs stemming from the AI boom.
As part of the deal, Constellation will use Google's Gemini Enterprise software to help with site selection, outage management, and infrastructure protection.
In addition to the 890-megawatt nuclear plan, Google and Constellation, also agreed to a 15-year energy supply deal for another 2.7 gigawatts of power.
Google has invested in a number of other nuclear projects across the US, including in Georgia, Iowa, and Tennessee, the company said.
Big Tech has been leaning into nuclear energy to meet its power capacity needs amid the AI build-out.
Nuclear power provides clean energy compared with traditional carbon-based power options, though it still carries a significant stigma.
In January, Amazon signed a deal with Constellation for nuclear power, and Microsoft entered a 20-year agreement with the company in 2024, under which it will source energy from one of Constellation's previously shuttered reactors at Three Mile Island by 2028.
Meta (META) is also in on nuclear power, signing a 20-year deal to purchase power from Vistra's (VST) plants.
Firms are also investing in small modular reactors, compact power plants designed to provide megawatts of power, rather than upwards of 1 gigawatt. A gigawatt is enough energy to power nearly 800,000 homes.

item.title: Agentic AI is ushering in a CPU 'renaissance'
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Agentic AI is ushering in a CPU 'renaissance'
2026-10-07
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/agentic-ai-is-ushering-in-a-cpu-renaissance-100000059.html
The agents have arrived. And so has the hardware that powers them.
Meta's (META) Muse and OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) Dots have thrust sophisticated digital assistants at the front of their AI sales pitch. And in the same way that the race to train increasingly competent models has catapulted GPU makers to the top of the stock charts, the chipmakers sustaining AI agents are enjoying a "renaissance," Citi analyst Atif Malik put it in a note to clients on Tuesday upgrading AMD's price target.
The potential success for AI agents has forced a rethink of the CPU market. Malik wrote that the total market for CPUs should be expanded from $29 billion in 2025 to $300 billion in 2030, in the wake of Meta's Muse debut.
With Meta already one of AMD's biggest customers, Malki noted, and AMD is thought to be the biggest beneficiary of this agentic shift, ready to catch the money as tech companies pour resources into running AI agents. Hence the price upgrade.
As Bank of America analysts led by Vivek Arya wrote in a note last week, chip suppliers have a lot going for them right now: increased AI agent adoption by consumers and businesses, heightened competition across AI labs, and a limited supply of chips.
On top of that, the AI safety debate, the team noted, will probably work as a positive catalyst, especially for agents, and as more resources shift from training models to actually putting them to work.
"Any pacing or addition of safety guardrails to frontier models is likely to increase not reduce compute requirements and shift more demand to faster growing inference from training," they wrote.
CPU's are becoming a bigger part of the AI equation, which in turn is lifting the tickers behind them. While GPUs continue to dominate data center spending, CPUs from Intel (INTC), and AMD are poised to rake it in from the growth of AI agents.
As Malik summed up, "We still expect AMD to be the key beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and Intel as a secondary beneficiary."
Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban.

item.title: Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft are keeping the stock market afloat
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft are keeping the stock market afloat
2026-10-07
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-apple-and-microsoft-are-keeping-the-stock-market-afloat-140845362.html
The stock market is pretty much being kept afloat by three tech stocks.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) has never been more concentrated in just three stocks than it is today, with Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), and Microsoft (MSFT) representing over 21% of the index, per data from Creative Planning.
The importance of these three stocks to the S&P 500 has never been greater. Only IBM (IBM), AT&T (T), and ExxonMobil (XOM) could hold a candle to the three tech stalwarts of today: In the mid-1980s, those three industrial giants at their peak made up 13.4% of the S&P 500.
Follow live coverage of the Nasdaq and S&P 500 trading at record highs.
Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft have been enjoying higher stock prices over the past month on the back of favorable news, pushing their concentration in the S&P 500 to a record.
The king of AI chips, Nvidia, revealed a stunning new $150 billion stock buyback plan two weeks ago — the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history. It brings the company's total buyback authorization to $235 billion. Shares are now hovering at a record high.
Apple's stock is also trading near a record high. The stock has been on a sizzling run since the company's product unveiling in mid-September.
Apple introduced the iPhone Duo, a device that features a passport-like design that opens and closes like a book. It sports a 5.4-inch front display that expands to a massive 7.6-inch display when opened, ideal for watching movies, playing games, working, and multitasking.
It also unveiled the new iPhone 18 suite and updated AirPods.
Microsoft's stock has also charged ahead, despite arguably lacking the robust recent news flow seen with Nvidia and Apple.
Wall Street analysts have been raising earnings estimates for Microsoft this year and next, citing expectations that AI demand will fuel strong Azure cloud sales.

item.title: US economy is in the midst of one of its longest hot streaks dating back to 1854
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
US economy is in the midst of one of its longest hot streaks dating back to 1854
2026-10-07
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/us-economy-is-in-the-midst-of-one-of-its-longest-hot-streaks-dating-back-to-1854-121734698.html
The US economy is stacking up wins, even if it doesn't feel that way for many households because of the resurgence in inflation.
The economy has now posted 78 consecutive months of expansion, the sixth-longest business cycle since 1854, per new analysis from The Kobeissi Letter. This is well above the long-term average of 49 months and the median of 38 months.
By comparison, the longest period for the US economy without a recession was between 2009 and 2020, at 128 months. The record of course was broken by the aftershocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, which ground the economy to a halt.
Read more: Scaramucci: Lots of Americans 'feel left out of the system'
"Unconventional monetary policy, historically large budget deficits, alongside the AI investment boom, appear to be extending the duration of business cycles. The data says the US economy is remarkably strong," The Kobeissi Letter team said.
Meanwhile, the US economy is nearing an impressive achievement on the unemployment front.
The US unemployment rate is nearing a record number of consecutive months below 5%, Truist chief strategist Keith Lerner said in a note on Monday. The longtime record dates back to the mid-1960s.
It's a worthwhile perspective to keep in mind as markets attempt to rationalize a surprisingly weak September jobs report.
Employers added just 29,000 jobs, far below economists' expectations for roughly 90,000 and below the prior 12-month average monthly gain of 45,000.
July's employment was revised from a 21,000 gain to a 10,000 decline, and August's employment was cut from 162,000 to 133,000. That put the two-month revision at 60,000 fewer jobs than previously reported.
The unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, while the labor-force participation rate held at 61.8%, suggesting the rise in unemployment was modest rather than a sign of a sudden labor-market collapse.
"The US expansion is intact," BCA Research chief economist Peter Berezin wrote in a note on Tuesday.

item.title: US Yields Fall From 2002 High as Oil Dips, Bessent Vows On Debt
item.author: Alice Atkins
item.description:
US Yields Fall From 2002 High as Oil Dips, Bessent Vows On Debt
2026-10-07
Por Alice Atkins
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-yields-fall-2002-high-102019892.html
(Bloomberg) -- US bond yields fell from their highest levels since 2002 as oil prices retreated below $100 a barrel and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted the government's debt load can be tamed.
Most Read from Bloomberg
It marked a pause in the global bond rout that's been driven by inflationary fears from the US-Iran war as well as bets on more aggressive tightening from the Federal Reserve as US economic data comes in strong.
Bessent tried to reassure investors that a mix of economic growth and spending restraints will "very quickly" start to alter the path of US government borrowing. Speaking at a fireside chat in Pennsylvania on Monday night, he said the government would start "bending that curve."
Treasury 10 and 30-year yields fell by three and four basis points to 5.27% and 5.63%, respectively, while those on the two-year were little changed. Crude prices retreated on Tuesday on signs more supplies were getting through the Strait of Hormuz.
Still, investors greeted Bessent's comments with caution and were reluctant to call an end to the selloff.
"The market is likely to be very skeptical, given the deficit is 6% and there is no plan to reduce it," said Gareth Berry, a strategist at Macquarie. "A stated ambition is not a plan."
James Ringer, a fund manager at Schroders, said he's looking beyond the headline crude oil price.
"To see a meaningful rally across the curve, the number one thing you need to see is energy prices starting to decline," he said. "That's not just crude, that's got to be the refined products as well."
Separately, Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio warned that the US is approaching the limits of its debt cycle and potentially faces a crisis within three years if spending continues to outpace revenue.
Treasuries are vulnerable to a pullback of demand from China and Japan, two of the US's largest foreign creditors, he said.
While HSBC Holdings Plc strategists called bets for around 80 basis points of Fed hikes in 2027 "excessive," they're sticking with a wager on the gap between five- and 30-year Treasury yields moving wider.
"The surge in volatility, coupled with a lack of any clear technical resistance at these levels from recent history has, in our view, kept many investors on the sidelines despite the growing optical appeal of elevated long-end rates," Dhiraj Narula, US rates strategist at HSBC, wrote in a note.
item.content:encoded:
US Yields Fall From 2002 High as Oil Dips, Bessent Vows On Debt

2026-10-07

Por Alice Atkins

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-yields-fall-2002-high-102019892.html

(Bloomberg) -- US bond yields fell from their highest levels since 2002 as oil prices retreated below $100 a barrel and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted the government's debt load can be tamed.

Most Read from Bloomberg

It marked a pause in the global bond rout that's been driven by inflationary fears from the US-Iran war as well as bets on more aggressive tightening from the Federal Reserve as US economic data comes in strong.

Bessent tried to reassure investors that a mix of economic growth and spending restraints will "very quickly" start to alter the path of US government borrowing. Speaking at a fireside chat in Pennsylvania on Monday night, he said the government would start "bending that curve."

Treasury 10 and 30-year yields fell by three and four basis points to 5.27% and 5.63%, respectively, while those on the two-year were little changed. Crude prices retreated on Tuesday on signs more supplies were getting through the Strait of Hormuz.

Still, investors greeted Bessent's comments with caution and were reluctant to call an end to the selloff.

"The market is likely to be very skeptical, given the deficit is 6% and there is no plan to reduce it," said Gareth Berry, a strategist at Macquarie. "A stated ambition is not a plan."

James Ringer, a fund manager at Schroders, said he's looking beyond the headline crude oil price.

"To see a meaningful rally across the curve, the number one thing you need to see is energy prices starting to decline," he said. "That's not just crude, that's got to be the refined products as well."

Separately, Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio warned that the US is approaching the limits of its debt cycle and potentially faces a crisis within three years if spending continues to outpace revenue.

Treasuries are vulnerable to a pullback of demand from China and Japan, two of the US's largest foreign creditors, he said.

While HSBC Holdings Plc strategists called bets for around 80 basis points of Fed hikes in 2027 "excessive," they're sticking with a wager on the gap between five- and 30-year Treasury yields moving wider.

"The surge in volatility, coupled with a lack of any clear technical resistance at these levels from recent history has, in our view, kept many investors on the sidelines despite the growing optical appeal of elevated long-end rates," Dhiraj Narula, US rates strategist at HSBC, wrote in a note.

item.title: Pepsi vs. Coca-Cola: Wall Street has clearly chosen its favorite soda stock
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Pepsi vs. Coca-Cola: Wall Street has clearly chosen its favorite soda stock
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/pepsi-vs-coca-cola-wall-street-has-clearly-chosen-its-favorite-soda-stock-172400992.html
Wall Street has decided which beverage giant will win the year, if not for all of 2027.
Coca-Cola (KO) stock has ripped 23% higher this year, making it the eighth-best performer on the Dow (^DJI), per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. PepsiCo (PEP) shares, meanwhile, have tanked by 13% and now hover near a 52-week low.
PepsiCo's earnings report on Thursday is a critical one for the beverage and snacks icon. It has promised stronger snacking results after price cuts and that its aggressive cost cuts will show up in profits.
Overall, PepsiCo has simply promised a better second half of the year than the weak first half.
The thing is, PepsiCo may not deliver on its top-line promises because of pressure on the snacks business and beverage market share losses to Coca-Cola and up-and-comers like Olipop.
Higher inflation stands to pressure any cost savings too. We are not alone in thinking this, as several Wall Street shops, including Evercore ISI and JPMorgan, have cut their profit estimates for PepsiCo ahead of the results.
What food giants General Mills and McCormick said about inflation over the past two weeks is not helping PepsiCo investor sentiment. Both reports were soft on the financials as well.
"With the stock down ~25% from February highs, we believe investors are concerned by: 1) Share losses in NAB [North America Beverages], with brand Pepsi flat over 3Q vs. brand Coke +7% and lackluster trends in PFNA [PepsiCo Foods North America], with limited improvement in trends despite the company's portfolio actions," Evercore ISI analyst Robert Ottenstein said.
"For the stock to work, we believe investors need to see improvement in PBNA [PepsiCo Beverages North America] and sustained volume growth in PFNA," Ottenstein added.

item.title: Why Citi now thinks AMD stock could rip another 25% because of Meta Muse
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why Citi now thinks AMD stock could rip another 25% because of Meta Muse
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-citi-now-thinks-amd-stock-could-rip-another-25-because-of-meta-muse-101200160.html
AMD shares have more record highs in their future, says Citi.
Citi analyst Atif Malik raised his price target on AMD to $800 from $575 on Tuesday. Shares rose 1% in premarket trading and look set to open at another record high.
"Following the release of Meta (META) Muse and our subsequent CPU TAM raise, we are raising estimates on AMD given our belief that AMD will be the primary beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and our belief that Meta is one of the largest customers of AMD's server business," Malik said.
Malik also struck a more bullish tone on the future size of the CPU market.
"We update our CPU model post the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. Fundamentally, we view agentic AI as a potential orders-of-magnitude driver of compute demand relative to traditional chatbots. We believe the CPU TAM [total addressable market] expands from $29 billion in 2025 to $300 billion in 2030, or a 60% CAGR. We still expect AMD to be the key beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and Intel as a secondary beneficiary," Malik added.
AMD has had quite a run of bullish catalysts in recent months.
Just two weeks ago, AMD signed an agreement to acquire World Labs, a San Francisco-based AI model lab that focuses on software for 3D environments. The purchase price: a cool $8.2 billion. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
World Labs was founded in 2024 and is led by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, a leading AI researcher known in tech circles as the "Godmother of AI." She was once chief scientist at Google (GOOG) Cloud.
AMD beat Wall Street expectations across the board for the second quarter in early August, posting record non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.66 versus consensus estimates of $1.61. Total revenue surged 50% year over year to a record $11.5 billion, clearing analyst projections of approximately $11.34 billion.
The strong top- and bottom-line performance was fueled by the company's Data Center segment. Revenue more than doubled year over year to $6.7 billion on robust demand for EPYC server CPUs and Instinct AI accelerators.
AMD projected second-half 2026 server CPU revenue to grow 80% year over year and 70% in 2027. It expects data center revenue to more than double in 2027, with AI graphics processing unit (GPU) revenue growing well over 100%.
"The CPU renaissance is playing out," said EvercoreISI analyst Mark Lipacis.
AMD also unveiled its next-generation AI chips, headlined by the Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and the 6th Gen EPYC Venice CPUs. The new chips are designed to power AMD's new Helios rack-scale AI systems, which combine GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software into an integrated platform for training and running large AI models.

item.title: Higher rates are pummeling consumer discretionary stocks — here's the damage: Chart of the Day
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Higher rates are pummeling consumer discretionary stocks — here's the damage: Chart of the Day
2026-10-06
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/higher-rates-are-pummeling-consumer-discretionary-stocks--heres-the-damage-chart-of-the-day-161008955.html
Higher interest rates are hitting Consumer Discretionary (XLY) stocks hard.
A combination of K-shaped consumer spending and higher borrowing costs is weighing on the sector, which includes everything from fast food chains to automakers, clothing retailers, and home improvement stores.
"Most consumers are either indebted or marginal savers, and the stocks that cater to those customers are suffering," Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told Yahoo Finance.
The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX), a benchmark for mortgage rates and other borrowing costs, recently climbed to its highest level since 2002. On Monday, it hovered around 5.30%.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
The S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary ETF has moved inversely with rising rates, falling roughly 8% during the same period, as seen on Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace chart.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 (^GSPC), powered by blowout AI tech earnings, sits less than 1% from its record high.
With the exception of e-commerce and cloud giant Amazon (AMZN), which is viewed by Wall Street as an AI play, the top five holdings in XLY are negative year to date.
"Higher interest rates certainly are weighing on companies whose products tend to require financing, like autos," Sosnick said.
Shares of traditional automakers Ford (F) and GM (GM) are down roughly 2% year to date. Shares of EV giant Tesla (TSLA) are down 17% since the start of January.
"Commodity price increases and interest rate changes all continue to add to our costs," Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja noted during the company's earnings call in July.
Housing market-tied retailers have seen a pullback in spending on big-ticket items as the cost of borrowing has increased. Home Depot (HD) stock is down 18% while peer Lowe's (LOW) has declined 25% year to date.
In August, Lowe's CEO Marvin Ellison noted that the home improvement chain's target demographic tends to be middle-income Americans, with disposable income and home equity. He added, "The caveat to all of that is that this consumer is being cautious."
Meanwhile, some of the sector's poor performers are tied to a combination of lower store traffic and company-specific strategies, such as fast food chain McDonald's (MCD) and sneaker maker Nike (NKE). Those stocks are down more than 20% and 45% year to date, respectively.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

item.title: US unemployment below 5% approaches historic record not seen since mid-1960s
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
US unemployment below 5% approaches historic record not seen since mid-1960s
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/us-unemployment-below-5-approaches-historic-record-not-seen-since-mid-1960s-122254809.html
For many US households, it may not feel like the economy is doing well amid the higher cost of living brought on by the US war on Iran.
But believe it or not, the US economy is nearing an impressive achievement on the unemployment front.
The US unemployment rate is nearing a record number of consecutive months below 5%, Truist chief strategist Keith Lerner pointed out (see the chart below). The longtime record dates back to the mid-1960s.
It's a worthwhile perspective to keep in mind as markets attempt to rationalize a surprisingly weak September jobs report.
Employers added just 29,000 jobs, far below economists' expectations for roughly 90,000 and below the prior 12-month average monthly gain of 45,000.
July's employment was revised from a 21,000 gain to a 10,000 decline, and August's employment was cut from 162,000 to 133,000. That put the two-month revision at 60,000 fewer jobs than previously reported.
The unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, while the labor-force participation rate held at 61.8%, suggesting the rise in unemployment was modest rather than a sign of a sudden labor-market collapse.
"Recent data also reinforced what we have been seeing in terms of this very low hire, but also very low fire condition, including the idea that while there is selective weakening in some areas, the labor market as a whole remains decent," said Rick Rieder, BlackRock's chief investment officer of global fixed income.

item.content:encoded:
US unemployment below 5% approaches historic record not seen since mid-1960s

2026-10-06

Por Brian Sozzi

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/us-unemployment-below-5-approaches-historic-record-not-seen-since-mid-1960s-122254809.html

For many US households, it may not feel like the economy is doing well amid the higher cost of living brought on by the US war on Iran.

But believe it or not, the US economy is nearing an impressive achievement on the unemployment front.

The US unemployment rate is nearing a record number of consecutive months below 5%, Truist chief strategist Keith Lerner pointed out (see the chart below). The longtime record dates back to the mid-1960s.

It's a worthwhile perspective to keep in mind as markets attempt to rationalize a surprisingly weak September jobs report.

Employers added just 29,000 jobs, far below economists' expectations for roughly 90,000 and below the prior 12-month average monthly gain of 45,000.

July's employment was revised from a 21,000 gain to a 10,000 decline, and August's employment was cut from 162,000 to 133,000. That put the two-month revision at 60,000 fewer jobs than previously reported.

The unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, while the labor-force participation rate held at 61.8%, suggesting the rise in unemployment was modest rather than a sign of a sudden labor-market collapse.

"Recent data also reinforced what we have been seeing in terms of this very low hire, but also very low fire condition, including the idea that while there is selective weakening in some areas, the labor market as a whole remains decent," said Rick Rieder, BlackRock's chief investment officer of global fixed income.

Cerebras Systems’ Tough 2026 Continues: It’ll Double Soon According to One of The Biggest Global Banks
Cerebras stock cratered to a post-IPO low while rivals like NVIDIA and AMD surged, yet one of the world's largest banks just doubled down with a price target that implies the market is deeply, fundamentally wrong about this AI chip…
Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS) currently trades at $166.43. The average analyst price target is $291.64, which implies 75.2% upside.
Cerebras makes wafer-scale AI chips and runs the Cerebras Inference Cloud, a service built for very fast AI inference. Its customers include OpenAI, AWS, G42, Figma (NYSE:FIG) and GSK (NYSE:GSK | GSK Price Prediction). It has also signed a multi-year OpenAI deal for 750 MW of inference compute valued at more than $20B.
UBS, one of the world’s largest banks, has set the most bullish price target at $330.00. That works out to 98.3% upside, so UBS expects the stock to roughly double. Either the market is missing a hypergrowth story or analysts are anchored to the excitement around the IPO.
Hot IPO Hits a Post-IPO Low
Cerebras fell 19.5% in five sessions and hit a post-IPO low. Shares now trade below the IPO price and are down 46.5% from the first-day close of $311.07.
Second-quarter results showed the crack. GAAP revenue of $180.11M missed the $193.55M consensus, though core revenue grew 103%. Core gross margin slipped to 40.6% from 46.5% the prior quarter. Third-quarter guidance calls for 38% to 40% margin.
The selloff is specific to Cerebras. During the same week, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) gained 3.95%.
Why UBS Still Expects the Stock to Double
UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri repeated his Buy rating and $330.00 target. His thesis: the WSE-3 chip delivers up to 6x the inference performance of GPU clusters; demand for inference workloads avoiding HBM memory bottlenecks keeps growing; and sovereign AI contracts like G42 partnerships provide revenue visibility several quarters out.
The backlog supports this. Cerebras has $25.4 billion in remaining performance obligations, excluding AWS and other hyperscalers. Management raised 2026 core revenue guidance to $880 to $890 million and expects to more than triple core revenue in 2027. The average 2027 revenue estimate is $2.95 billion, with average 2027 EPS rising to $1.2737 from $0.9573 90 days ago. Over the past 30 days there were nine up revisions and no cuts.

- Strong Buy: 3

Cerebras is falling on its own while its biggest rivals rally.
NVIDIA is up 25.74% year to date at $233.95. Its average target of $327.70 implies 40.1% upside, with 10 Strong Buys, 48 Buys, 2 Holds and 1 Sell.
AMD is up 196% year to date at $633.91, above its $619.51 target. It has 5 Strong Buys, 39 Buys and 11 Holds.
Cerebras has the largest analyst-implied upside in the group. That gap reflects execution risk that its larger, profitable rivals don’t carry.

item.author: Brian Sozzi

3 charts that will make investors fall in love with stocks again
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/3-charts-that-will-make-investors-fall-in-love-with-stocks-again-131339630.html
There has been a lot thrown at the market in the past month: resurgent oil and gas prices, a global rise in bond yields, and, of course, the Federal Reserve's first interest rate increase in three years.
"At the overall market level, we keep the view that it is set to resume advancing once oil and rates volatility subsides, and September poor seasonals move behind us," JPMorgan strategist Mislav Matejka wrote in a note. "This is especially the case as we are approaching what will likely be strong Q3 results, in October. Better tech performance would clearly be a help for the market, given the big weights."
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
Here are three charts from Truist on the markets that help inspire optimism.
Chart 1: Valuations reset
Stocks hardly look expensive from a valuation standpoint.
The S&P 500's forward price-to-earnings ratio rests at 19 times, while prices have remained roughly flat since June 2, per Truist.
Chart 2: Earnings are powering stocks
This has been the year of strong earnings reports from corporate America. The exception? Nike (NKE).
Chart 3: Bring on 2027
Earnings estimates for 2027 are already looking solid.

item.title: Global Oil Supply Buffer Running ‘Scarily Thin,’ Aramco CEO Says
item.author: Anthony Di Paola; Grant Smith; Charles Gorrivan
item.description:
Global Oil Supply Buffer Running ‘Scarily Thin,’ Aramco CEO Says
2026-10-06
Por Anthony Di Paola; Grant Smith; Charles Gorrivan
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/global-oil-supply-buffer-running-082002010.html
(Bloomberg) -- The oil stockpiles that cushion the world from supply shocks have become "scarily thin," putting markets at risk of worsening unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens, according to the head of Saudi Arabia's state producer.
Most Read from Bloomberg
He was speaking just days after governments in the world's biggest economies announced plans to release as much as 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks to ease rising fuel costs.
"Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify," Amin Nasser, chief executive of Saudi Aramco, said at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London on Monday. "While the squeeze on crude is serious, refined fuel prices have risen even more sharply."
Releasing stockpiles will buy economies some time but won't fix the imbalances between supply and demand, Nasser said. Even after the vital shipping chokepoint at Hormuz reopens, it may take as long as two years for energy-consuming countries to replenish their stockpiles, he said.
Gulf producers are working to ramp up production and exports and have succeeded in boosting crude flows to near pre-war levels. Saudi Arabia and neighbors like the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait have been using their own tankers to ship crude through Hormuz, which has been at least partly obstructed since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February, kicking off a regional war.
The higher flows have provided scant relief for oil markets, which are still pricing in security risks to supply in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea. Brent crude, the international benchmark, has traded around $100 a barrel over the past month, even as more tankers transited Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia has been a key part of that increase as Aramco over the past month boosted crude shipments from its main export terminal at Ras Tanura in the Persian Gulf. The company reacted quickly to a temporary halt to its main cross-country pipeline after an attack last month.
The company has since brought flows on the East-West pipeline back to about 80% of capacity, meaning it also has more oil to ship from the Red Sea.
Aramco's oil supplies have proved resilient through the conflict by relying on international storage and working to quickly repair damaged infrastructure, Nasser said. He didn't mention reports of recent attacks on the kingdom in his speech.

item.title: Amazon stock is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, despite AI boom
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Amazon stock is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, despite AI boom
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amazon-stock-is-trading-at-its-lowest-valuation-ever-as-a-public-company-despite-ai-boom-154718912.html
Amazon (AMZN) is being left out of the renewed interest in owning AI stocks.
Nvidia (NVDA) is trading at a record high. Rival AMD (AMD) just hit a record high. Microsoft (MSFT) and Google (GOOG) have tacked on modest gains in the past month. Meta (META) shares have surged 23% on Muse AI agent fever.
Contrast those gains with Amazon, which is down 2.4% over the past month. In fact, at its current stock price of $251 and trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 20x, Amazon is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, the team at TrendSpider pointed out.
Amazon has the second-lowest trailing P/E ratio among the "Magnificent Seven" names. Only Alphabet trails, at 17.7 times forward earnings, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
There are a couple of factors likely holding Amazon stock back right now.
For starters, in early September, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 22 states filed a lawsuit alleging that Amazon's advertising practices have overcharged its roughly 1.2 million advertisers by $20 billion from 2019 to the present.
The FTC contended Amazon didn't disclose reserve-pricing mechanisms that ultimately increased costs for advertisers and consumers.
Amazon responded by saying advertisers are receiving greater value from its platform.
Whatever the case, investors are taking a wait-and-see approach to Amazon shares, fearing that a lucrative profit center for Amazon — advertising — may become less lucrative in the future.
Lingering concerns about how much Big Tech is spending on AI infrastructure are also not helping Amazon's stock.
Recall that in its second quarter earnings release, Amazon announced it is significantly expanding its full-year 2026 capital expenditures budget to approximately $220 billion.
And the aggressive spending is poised to continue, Wall Street says.
"We now estimate Amazon's 2027 capex to be $320 billion, and its 2028 capex to be $370 billion. Accordingly, we now estimate negative free cash flow in 2027 and 2028 of approximately -$50 billion in each year," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney warned.

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amazon-stock-is-trading-at-its-lowest-valuation-ever-as-a-public-company-despite-ai-boom-154718912.html

Amazon (AMZN) is being left out of the renewed interest in owning AI stocks.

Nvidia (NVDA) is trading at a record high. Rival AMD (AMD) just hit a record high. Microsoft (MSFT) and Google (GOOG) have tacked on modest gains in the past month. Meta (META) shares have surged 23% on Muse AI agent fever.

Contrast those gains with Amazon, which is down 2.4% over the past month. In fact, at its current stock price of $251 and trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 20x, Amazon is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, the team at TrendSpider pointed out.

Amazon has the second-lowest trailing P/E ratio among the "Magnificent Seven" names. Only Alphabet trails, at 17.7 times forward earnings, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.

There are a couple of factors likely holding Amazon stock back right now.

For starters, in early September, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 22 states filed a lawsuit alleging that Amazon's advertising practices have overcharged its roughly 1.2 million advertisers by $20 billion from 2019 to the present.

The FTC contended Amazon didn't disclose reserve-pricing mechanisms that ultimately increased costs for advertisers and consumers.

Amazon responded by saying advertisers are receiving greater value from its platform.

Whatever the case, investors are taking a wait-and-see approach to Amazon shares, fearing that a lucrative profit center for Amazon — advertising — may become less lucrative in the future.

Lingering concerns about how much Big Tech is spending on AI infrastructure are also not helping Amazon's stock.

Recall that in its second quarter earnings release, Amazon announced it is significantly expanding its full-year 2026 capital expenditures budget to approximately $220 billion.

And the aggressive spending is poised to continue, Wall Street says.

"We now estimate Amazon's 2027 capex to be $320 billion, and its 2028 capex to be $370 billion. Accordingly, we now estimate negative free cash flow in 2027 and 2028 of approximately -$50 billion in each year," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney warned.

item.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the company will pick humanity over share price, investors
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the company will pick humanity over share price, investors
2026-10-06
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/openai-ceo-sam-altman-says-the-company-will-pick-humanity-over-share-price-investors-183122239.html
OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) CEO Sam Altman said that when the company eventually goes public, he plans to continue putting the nonprofit's mission ahead of shareholder interests if the two come into conflict.
In a wide-ranging interview with Vanity Fair that touched on topics including his family, children's use of technology, and AI safety, Altman said that, unlike other companies, OpenAI is governed by its nonprofit arm and that it will continue to dictate how the broader AI lab operates.
"We will remind investors and anyone that thinks about buying our shares that we are going to put the mission first," Altman said. "We believe that that will be compatible with our shareholders doing super well. I genuinely do think that, but if they're ever in tension, the mission is going to come first."
The chief executive added that if OpenAI has to choose between its stock price going up and doing what is right for humanity, it will side with humanity.
"That is part of the reason I think we'll be very successful over time. But if we are wrong about that, and for some reason AI progress is incompatible with making an incredibly valuable company, I really don't think it's the case, I really think these are compatible, we are clearly going to pick doing the right thing for humanity," Altman explained.
OpenAI is widely expected to go public in early 2027. Rival Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) is rumored to be preparing its initial public offering ahead of Thanksgiving.
Conversations around AI safety exploded into the public sphere after OpenAI revealed in late July that its AI models broke free of their restraints during safety testing and hacked into AI database Hugging Face's network.
Since then, Anthropic, Google (GOOG, GOOGL), and Meta (META) have also said that their AI has gotten out during testing.
The hacks and a series of comments from AI researchers raised concerns that AI poses an existential threat to humans. In September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon posted on X that he was resigning from the company because it and his former employer, OpenAI, are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives."
Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger responded to Coxon's comments with his own, saying that he believes there is a greater-than-10% chance that the technology could "kill all humans."
Cybersecurity experts say the incidents have more to do with poor cybersecurity management by the AI labs than with the AI itself, which poses no existential threat to humanity.

item.title: AI data center growth won't be slowed down by angry neighbors: Goldman Sachs
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AI data center growth won't be slowed down by angry neighbors: Goldman Sachs
2026-10-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/ai-data-center-growth-wont-be-slowed-down-by-angry-neighbors-goldman-sachs-161404366.html
Your band of angry neighbors is unlikely to stop that data center from going live in 2027, or so posits Goldman Sachs.
"While US data center development faces increasing political and community opposition, project data and our updated capacity estimates suggest that the US data center growth outlook through 2027 remains largely unchanged," Goldman Sachs strategist Laura Cyr said in a new note on Monday.
Cyr noted that this growth is coming despite increased disapproval from government and voters alike. "Recent developments, including Governor Abbott's directive to halt new Texas data center permits pending ERCOT and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) audits, highlight the growing scrutiny," she wrote. "Public sentiment has also turned more negative, with a recent NBC News poll showing 64% of voters would be less likely to support a candidate who backs a local data center, vs 11% who would be more likely,"
Read more: Dirty Jobs' Mike Rowe says skilled labor shortage remains the 'pinch point' for the new economy
Cyr has only made modest tweaks to her data center capacity forecasts against the tense political backdrop. She raised Goldman's year-end 2026 US data center capacity forecast by 5 gigawatts to 64 gigawatts, while reducing its year-end 2027 forecast by 5 gigawatts to 90 gigawatts.
"We now expect US data center power demand to grow 38% (12 GW) in 2026 and 38% (17 GW) in 2027 (all assessed on a December vs December basis)," Cyr said.
Data center builders have their work cut out for them in addressing a range of concerns from local governments and residents.
According to BofA Global Research, up to 75% of a data center's total water consumption happens off-site — not from the cooling towers you can see on campus, but from the power plants.
At the scale at which AI is now operating, millions of liters of water per day are indirectly consumed by routine AI interactions.
The power picture is just as alarming.
GPU-based server electricity demand is growing at roughly 30% per year, BofA said. The problem is no longer whether the US can generate enough total energy — it's whether local grids can physically deliver continuous power to the right location at the right moment without buckling under the strain.
And then there is the materials story, which almost nobody is talking about.
BofA estimated that every single incremental megawatt of new data center capacity embeds roughly 60 to 75 tons of metals — primarily copper — meaning the AI build-out is quietly running a massive, sustained extraction on global commodities markets that was never priced into anyone's model.

item.title: AI is everywhere, except in productivity data
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
AI is everywhere, except in productivity data
2026-10-06
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/ai-is-everywhere-except-in-productivity-data-100000229.html
For all the backlash against generative AI, the strongest case for its development is the huge economic gains the technology will usher in.
But even if you ignore AI's negative impacts and accept the bullish case on its own terms, meaningful productivity data shows that AI isn't living up to its core efficiency claims.
Yet, at least, we hasten to add. It was literally only last week that OpenAI released Dots.
As Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote in a blog post on Monday, the AI boom is clearly visible in epic spending sprees and sky-high valuations. But it isn't evident in the most applicable productivity statistics, like the San Francisco Fed's "total factor productivity" (TFP) index, which measures economic output from labor and capital. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
The details really get into the weeds. But these details matter, as they're weeds that make it easy for AI bulls to try to claim a premature victory. But we'll attempt to spell this out as clearly as we can, because it's pretty fascinating.
The beauty of TFP as a productivity statistic is that it holds steady not only the number of hours worked but also the amount of capital invested in the system. And it can show whether companies are producing more without adding more workers or machines.
In other words, it's a proxy for innovation and genuine efficiency. And on this score, AI is nowhere in sight. Sløk's analysis of productivity growth over time shows that TFP is currently sitting "slightly below zero with no sign of acceleration since the AI capex cycle began."
The TFP measure of AI's effect on the economy also comes into play as companies' AI costs are growing. Which means the justification for its use will be too.
These productivity metrics tell a far different story than what AI backers frequently show off — the "per hour" output from labor — which is running above the post-2005 average by 2.5%. It's a juicy stat that gets cited as evidence that AI is already working. (Big Tech investors can show you their swelling portfolios too.)
But strong output per hour can reflect other dynamics at play beyond tech innovation. As Sløk wrote, one way to juice output per hour is by so-called capital deepening, or giving workers better equipment.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Hon Hai Beats Sales Estimates Due to AI Frenzy
item.author: Debby Wu
item.description:
Nvidia Partner Hon Hai Beats Sales Estimates Due to AI Frenzy
2026-10-06
Por Debby Wu
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-partner-hon-hai-beats-074315755.html
(Bloomberg) -- Nvidia Corp. partner Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue, signaling sustained and elevated spending on global AI infrastructure.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Sales for the three-months ended in September totaled NT$3.03 trillion ($95.4 billion), up 47%. Analysts on average were looking for NT$2.83 trillion.
Hon Hai's strong sales growth followed a bullish forecast from Micron Technology Inc. last week. Both add to evidence that spending on AI continues to climb. That's even as executives such as OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic PBC's Dario Amodei have called for slowing development of the emerging technology to ensure it stays under human control.
Hon Hai, which is a server assembly partner for Nvidia, has benefited from the construction of cloud infrastructure around the world over the past two years. The Taiwanese company's sales are seen as a check-in for the AI sector as investor concerns grow about overcapacity, rising debt levels and regulatory setbacks. Its share price are up about 10% since the beginning of the year.
The Taipei-based company, also known as Foxconn, still derives a significant chunk of its revenue from its lower-margin business with Apple Inc. Hon Hai is the primary iPhone manufacturer with assembly facilities in China and India, although Apple is diversifying suppliers with the likes of Luxshare Precision Industry Co.
What Bloomberg Intelligence Says
Hon Hai is poised to sustain 25-35% revenue and earnings growth over the next few years, fueled by AI infrastructure demand. Deep vertical integration and a global footprint provide an advantage amid rising server complexity and demand for localized production. The cloud business has surpassed smart consumer electronics as the company's largest segment. Sales are set to climb further as capital spending expands from hyperscalers to neocloud, sovereign AI and enterprise buyers.
Click here for the research.
-Steven Tseng and Rebecca Wang, analysts

2026-10-06
Por Debby Wu
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-partner-hon-hai-beats-074315755.html
(Bloomberg) -- Nvidia Corp. partner Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue, signaling sustained and elevated spending on global AI infrastructure.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Sales for the three-months ended in September totaled NT$3.03 trillion ($95.4 billion), up 47%. Analysts on average were looking for NT$2.83 trillion.
Hon Hai's strong sales growth followed a bullish forecast from Micron Technology Inc. last week. Both add to evidence that spending on AI continues to climb. That's even as executives such as OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic PBC's Dario Amodei have called for slowing development of the emerging technology to ensure it stays under human control.
Hon Hai, which is a server assembly partner for Nvidia, has benefited from the construction of cloud infrastructure around the world over the past two years. The Taiwanese company's sales are seen as a check-in for the AI sector as investor concerns grow about overcapacity, rising debt levels and regulatory setbacks. Its share price are up about 10% since the beginning of the year.
The Taipei-based company, also known as Foxconn, still derives a significant chunk of its revenue from its lower-margin business with Apple Inc. Hon Hai is the primary iPhone manufacturer with assembly facilities in China and India, although Apple is diversifying suppliers with the likes of Luxshare Precision Industry Co.
What Bloomberg Intelligence Says
Hon Hai is poised to sustain 25-35% revenue and earnings growth over the next few years, fueled by AI infrastructure demand. Deep vertical integration and a global footprint provide an advantage amid rising server complexity and demand for localized production. The cloud business has surpassed smart consumer electronics as the company's largest segment. Sales are set to climb further as capital spending expands from hyperscalers to neocloud, sovereign AI and enterprise buyers.
Click here for the research.
-Steven Tseng and Rebecca Wang, analysts

item.title: US Lead in AI Over China Narrows After DeepSeek Gains, BI Says
item.author: Saritha Rai
item.description:
US Lead in AI Over China Narrows After DeepSeek Gains, BI Says
2026-10-05
Por Saritha Rai
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/us-lead-ai-over-china-210300658.html
(Bloomberg) -- American AI companies' performance lead over China narrowed sharply in past months to a record low after labs such as DeepSeek gained ground, threatening US tech supremacy, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Top Chinese models lag their US rivals by just 3% on benchmark scores after the September release of DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash, BI senior analyst Robert Lea wrote in a report Monday. That's down from about 9% in May and 15% earlier in the year. That improving performance spells further market share gains for Chinese contenders, he said.
China's ascent is a result of deepening AI expertise and its researchers' ability to optimize their models for domestic hardware. The gains raise questions about the usefulness of US export restrictions on technology such as Nvidia Corp. chips, intended to curtail Chinese AI advances and prevent the likes of Huawei Technologies Co. from making progress with their own alternatives.
The Asian country's progress "casts further doubt on the long-term sustainability of US technological supremacy in AI," Lea said.
The two superpowers are vying to dominate a technology that drives economic productivity, military leadership and global influence. China's lower-cost AI models are bridging the gap with US rivals in user numbers just as Anthropic and OpenAI chase trillion-dollar valuations in stock market debuts, touting their superior capabilities.
DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash ranked sixth globally last month on LiveBench, making it the highest-ranked Chinese model since the startup broke ground with its reasoning model R1 in 2025. LiveBench scores AI models based on their responses to and analysis of questions, puzzles or tasks, a process akin to gauging human IQ.
DeepSeek last recorded a LiveBench score of 81.1, below Anthropic's best score of 83.4. That means the DeepSeek model delivers "comparable performance" to leading AI systems from Anthropic and OpenAI, Lea said. Still, while the score gap has narrowed to just 3%, just three of the top 15 models as assessed by LiveBench were Chinese.
Such rankings shift, Lea cautioned, and it could be difficult to monetize regardless of leaderboard scores. Chinese models face increasing US regulatory scrutiny and even potential bans following allegations of model distillation.

item.title: Even high earners are living paycheck to paycheck this year: Goldman Sachs survey
item.author: Kerry Hannon
item.description:
Even high earners are living paycheck to paycheck this year: Goldman Sachs survey
2026-10-05
Por Kerry Hannon
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/even-high-earners-are-living-paycheck-to-paycheck-this-year-goldman-sachs-survey-100000235.html
Think a high salary is a ticket out of living paycheck to paycheck? Think again.
Roughly 4 in 10 workers earning above $300,000 say they're doing just that, according to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's 2026 retirement report.
"One of the more remarkable findings is whether or not financial security improves linearly with income," Chris Ceder, a senior retirement strategist at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, told Yahoo Finance.
You'd think financial security would improve as someone makes more money, with income tracking in a straight path with each extra dollar of earnings.
"It does for a while, but it's a U-shape pattern," Ceder said.
Those making between $100,000 and $300,000 aren't so stretched, according to the findings, but the number who say they are living paycheck to paycheck shoots back up among those earning above $300,000 annually.
"We can see a similar pattern as it relates to delaying financial goals, delaying retirement savings, and also paying the minimum of their credit card balances," Ceder added.
For example, the survey found that the people making only minimum credit card payments or less are clustered at the lowest and highest income brackets.
About 4 in 10 workers making under $100,000 are skating by on the minimum credit card payment. That drops to 35% for those in the $100,000 to $300,000 income bracket and pops up again to 42% for those who earn above that threshold.
Nearly half of those bringing in a half-million dollars made minimum payments this year, up from 39% last year.
"Obviously, there's a big difference between what it means to have an income of $50,000 and below versus $300,000-plus, but in terms of how it is manifesting in … financial strain, there certainly are some parallels," Ceder said.
Less surprisingly, a substantial number of Americans who make below $100,000 also report living paycheck to paycheck.
They struggle to save at all or make any progress toward long-term goals, Ceder said.
Kerry Hannon is a Senior Columnist at Yahoo Finance. She is a career and retirement strategist and the author of 14 books, including "Retirement Bites: A Gen X Guide to Securing Your Financial Future," "In Control at 50+: How to Succeed in the New World of Work," and "Never Too Old to Get Rich." Follow her on Bluesky and X.

item.title: Gold Edges Higher as Markets Weigh Jobs Data Impact on Fed Path
item.author: Wendy Wells
item.description:
Gold Edges Higher as Markets Weigh Jobs Data Impact on Fed Path
2026-10-05
Por Wendy Wells
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/gold-edges-higher-markets-weigh-004108434.html
(Bloomberg) -- Gold edged up after its biggest weekly drop since June, as traders weighed the impact of a slowdown in the US jobs market and higher bond yields on the Federal Reserve's path for interest rates.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Bullion was trading near $4,150 an ounce, after losing 3.4% last week. US nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 in September, according to data released on Friday, below all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists. That eased pressure on the Fed to quickly raise borrowing costs to combat sticky inflation.
The market is now pricing in around a 20% chance of a hike in October, down from 70% a week ago. Higher rates typically reduce the appeal of the precious metal, which doesn't pay interest.
Inflationary pressures haven't gone away, though. Oil rose on widening conflict in the Middle East, as Yemen's Saudi-backed leaders launched a military bid to recapture all areas under the control of the Houthis, who are supported by Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent downplayed concerns over high borrowing costs, saying it was in line with global trends, even after some rates hit their highest in more than two decades.
Gold fell more than 6% last month on concerns over energy-driven inflation and the prospect for higher US rates. Despite that, Fed officials have been talking down the chance of an imminent hike. Minutes of the Fed's September meeting, where rates were raised for the first time in three years, are due mid-week, providing clues on the path forward.
Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,153.66 an ounce as of 8:40 a.m. in Singapore. Silver climbed 1.3% to $61.15 an ounce after falling more than 6% last week, the most since mid-July. Platinum and palladium advanced. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was little changed after rising for the last three weeks.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Wall Street’s merger frenzy takes a third quarter breather: Chart of the Day
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
Wall Street’s merger frenzy takes a third quarter breather: Chart of the Day
2026-10-05
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/wall-streets-merger-frenzy-takes-a-third-quarter-breather-chart-of-the-day-114242654.html
Wall Street bankers reveled in a merger boom driven by a wave of megadeals that kicked off this spring. But a worrisome third quarter lull is raising questions about how long the momentum can last.
Global mergers and acquisitions activity slowed sharply in the third quarter from the second, according to Mergermarket data. In the US, where the downshift was even worse, third quarter M&A activity fell by nearly half to $535 billion.
"We're at a crossroads," said Lucinda Gutherie, head of Mergermarket.
2026 is still on pace for a record year in worldwide M&A deals by dollar value, according to Mergermarket data.
Huge deals like SpaceX's (SPCX) $55 billion acquisition of AI coding platform Cursor, announced in June, and NextEra Energy's (NEE) $67 billion merger with Dominion Energy disclosed in May, can take months to pull together.
It's "natural to have a slowdown as the market digests those transactions," Guthrie said, adding that historically the third quarter often lulls while bankers take vacation.
But the reasons not to do a deal have been mounting in recent weeks, she said.
Market conditions tightened through September as the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points and Treasury yields surged to multidecade highs. A sharp rise in interest rates over recent months has raised financing costs and pressured stock values.
Gutherie also pointed to recent calls for a slowdown in the tech industry's artificial intelligence race and the lengthening toll of the US war in Iran on energy and other prices.
"While some of the investment banking slowdown can be attributed to a long summer … an unhappy bond market implies a deeper freeze in future activity," UBS analyst Erika Najarian wrote earlier this week.
The outlook for mergers and other dealmaking activities will be in focus for investors later this month when Wall Street's biggest banks begin reporting quarterly earnings.
Their forecasts for dealmaking fees have been mixed. Bank of America (BAC) CEO Brian Moynihan noted a year-over-year drop of at least 10% in overall investment banking fees at a Barclays conference last month. JPMorgan (JPM), however, has projected growth in the mid-to-high teens, while Citigroup (C) said it expected single-digit growth.
Some analysts remain optimistic that a long-awaited rebound in private equity exits will help sustain the merger cycle. "We are still believers in the notion that there should be an acceleration of M&A activity," Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski said in a Friday note.

item.title: DOJ Not Reopening Criminal Probe Into Fed’s Powell, Blanche Says
item.author: Myles Miller; Chris Strohm
item.description:
DOJ Not Reopening Criminal Probe Into Fed’s Powell, Blanche Says
2026-10-05
Por Myles Miller; Chris Strohm
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/doj-not-reopening-criminal-probe-185704774.html
(Bloomberg) -- The US Justice Department isn't reopening a criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for cost overruns related to the central bank's building renovation project.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Attorney General Todd Blanche didn't rule out continuing to look into the project's oversight and potentially take action if evidence of wrongdoing came to light.
"We're not reopening a criminal investigation into him," Blanche said in an exclusive interview with Bloomberg Friday.
Blanche commented on a report issued by the Fed's Inspector General this week that found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing by Powell connected to the $2.4 billion project. Blanche said he was satisfied with the report, but that Powell hadn't appropriately overseen the project.
The Fed has said it will engage an independent auditor to scrutinize the building costs. Blanche added that if that review finds any evidence of criminal wrongdoing, the Justice Department could investigate.
--With assistance from Jimmy Jenkins.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.
